charaInfo.talent_doc: [Filed by Spacetrek Collective: Startorch Academy Student Records] [Forte Examination Report: RA2326-G] Student Name: Sigrika Synchronist Qualification: Negative Forte Overview: Tests reveal a Rabelle's Curve with a pronounced periodic waveform. Therefore, the student is classified as a Congenital Resonator. Her Tacet Mark is located on her back. According to the pre-admission personal file and the student's own account, the student demonstrates exceptional aptitude in deciphering rune frequencies and converting them into usable power. However, she reports that this ability remains unstable and is highly dependent on her mental state as well as her depth of knowledge regarding particular runes. "In the field of rune deciphering, Sigrika displays a rare talent, one that may pose a significant risk to herself if not treated carefully."
charaInfo.talent_certification: Rabelle's Waveform test sample analysis shows high-amplitude, non-periodic fluctuation patterns. Partial waveform blurring is observed, along with visible abnormal waveforms. Conclusion: Resonant Criticality is within normal range. However, subject stability is poor, with a potential risk of Overclocking. Currently, Resonator Sigrika has no history of Overclocking, and her Rabelle's Curve remains stable. Routine psychological counseling is required. "Sigrika is too hard on herself. Honestly, if she just eased up a little, her Resonator stability would improve dramatically." "...Students like her are not uncommon at Startorch Academy. They come in thinking their talent means something. Then they realize that here, it just gives them an edge in a few courses. Nothing more." "Still, I don't want our students to feel defined by grades, talent, or ability. They deserve to see how much more the world has to offer."

stories.title: Her Family
stories.content:
"I'm back..."

The moment Sigrika closed the door, a round Kronapuff that could've been a ball launched itself into her arms, sending her stumbling back two steps.

"Hey, Crackle! Did you have fun at home?" she laughed, steadying herself. "You look bigger again. Have you been eating too much? Alright, alright, let go of me! Where's Mother? Wait, don't tell me. My nose already knows."

She dashed into the kitchen. The fatigue of the journey melted away the instant she spotted the pot of rich, bubbling Smoked Meat Stew.

"You're back?" her mother glanced over. "Look at you, filthy from head to toe. Off chasing birds with your friends again, were you? In a few days, you will receive the <te href=700010>Reactor Drive</te>'s blessing. After that, you'll be considered a grown-up. A Solsworn can't be seen running around like that."
"No, no! I was helping Aunt Astrid with her herd. That doesn't count as running around."

Her mother reached out and pinched her cheek. Sigrika winced and scrunched up her face. It only made her mother's smile soften.

"Alright, alright. Go wash your hands. We'll eat once your father gets home."
"Okay!"

Sigrika grinned. She washed her hands carefully, then took the plates and utensils from the cupboard and laid them out neatly on the table.
When her father returned, their small home welcomed a dinner that wasn't lavish, but was warm enough to fill the room.
At the table, Sigrika counted the little gifts her father had brought back—flower crowns, hairpins, clear bits of glass, and a few small blocks whose purpose she couldn't quite guess. As she tucked them away, her mother sighed and began to complain about his buying strange trinkets again. Her father scratched his head, fumbled for an explanation, then, catching Sigrika's eye, seized his chance to change the subject.

"So, feeling confident about the coming Trial?"
"Of course," Sigrika answered without hesitation.

She liked this. Being with her family. Even when her parents nagged and rambled, she never felt annoyed. She knew, deep down, that all of it came from love and their high expectations for her.

Her parents wanted her to become an outstanding <te href=700025>Solsworn</te>. They hoped she would use her talent to help others, and more than that, they hoped she would grow into an outstanding person. Sigrika knew how to live up to those expectations. That was why she studied runes every day. Learned something new every day. Even when exhaustion crept into her bones.

Still, as the Trial drew closer, she couldn't help but feel nervous.

"It's alright," her parents said. "Our little Sigrika will pass with flying colors. After that, you'll be heading to <te href=851069>Startorch Academy</te>. That place has trials of its own waiting for you."
"Mhm!" Sigrika nodded, pushing her anxiety out the front door along with the dust of the road. For now, she would just enjoy dinner. After all, the stew really smelled good.
"Oh, right, Mother," she added suddenly. "Has Crackle put on weight? I could barely pick it up."
"Ask your father."
"Papa?"
"Haha… I might have... fed it a bit more than a little."

stories.title: Her Gift
stories.content:
The rune unfolded before her eyes, like a sun rising into the sky.

Few people knew that runes were never meant to be flat symbols, but something with great depth—just like what she was witnessing now. This small sun rose and unfurled, spilling its light freely and generously onto everything around it.

Sigrika watched in silence. If she were asked to explain what was happening, she would just say that runes carry meaning. She was only interpreting that meaning and allowing it to manifest in the world.

"Only?" she thought to herself.

People called it her gift. As if she had been born able to read the True Names of runes, born able to draw on the power sealed inside them. And so, of course, she could apply this gift elsewhere, like calculating the paths of the stars, fulfilling everything a <te href=700025>Solsworn</te> was expected to do.
 
But... that was all it was. A gift.

A gift meant that this was the one place where she could give her all and nowhere else. She could recreate the True Names of runes, but she could not truly understand their essence. Why did runes hold such immense energy? What were those fleeting visions she sometimes glimpsed when touching them? And when she deciphered runes, what were those syllables hinting at, the ones she heard but could never understand? 

She didn't know.

Standing here now, waiting to be marked with the "blessing of the <te href=700010>Reactor Drive</te>," she held a quiet hope: that once the blessing was imprinted onto her, once she crossed this threshold into adulthood, understanding would come naturally to her. But of course, it didn't.

The rune merely unfolded before her eyes. Nothing more. Even if it shone like a sun.

This was what being "gifted" meant. It meant that it ended here and only here. Anything beyond that, she would have to seek out herself. See it for herself. Think it through on her own.

Even now, when she had no answers at all.

Even if this <ano=Rune>gift</ano> felt like a <ano=True Name>shadow</ano> cast upon her by some <ano=civilization>greater entity</ano>.

stories.title: Her Limits
stories.content:
The frostlands.

Sigrika exhaled softly, a plume of white drifting into the air as she watched the herderless <te href=700022>Exoswarm</te> roaming in the distance.

She had been trailing them all night.

It had taken her hours to pull the Exoswarm out of their extreme agitation. Now, they wandered the frostlands in loose, aimless loops, but Sigrika knew this was not a good sign. Something in their command and navigation units had malfunctioned, leaving them to trace one pointless circle after another. And sooner or later, without warning, they would spiral back into a frenzied rampage. When that happened, the nearest Royan settlement would be the first to suffer.

It was a riddle. And she didn't have much time left to solve it. But that was fine. She was ready.

"These True Names… Illuminate."

The next instant, runes flared to life across the Exoswarm, then detonated. The aimless circling stopped. And in its place came rage. The Exoswarm recalibrated as one, locked onto Sigrika, and charged. 

Their thunderous steps shattered the silence of the frostlands. The ground trembled beneath them. Sigrika tightened her grip on her dagger and began tracing runes in the air.

Calm. Focus. These were the absolute requirements when drawing and deciphering runes. Stroke by stroke, the runes formed before her. And all the while, the Exoswarm bore down, their fury heating the very air, melting the snow beneath their pounding steps.

Three... They carved deep, stretching grooves across the ice. Runes flickered on their bodies, but did nothing to slow them down. Driven by the single command to charge, they only accelerated, faster and faster—

Two... Sigrika tapped the final point with her blade. She vanished. At almost the same instant, every rune on the Exoswarm ignited, and Sigrika slipped between them, shuttling through their ranks on the paths her runes had carved.

One! The rune trap activated. Chain explosions erupted. Wind blades tore through the Exoswarm, cutting off their advance. And at the center of it all, Sigrika's dagger found its mark—the key to the riddle. When the shockwaves finally faded, she landed lightly, pulled forward by a <te href=700026>Soliskin</te>. Behind her, the Exoswarm herd that had raged all night finally fell silent, and the last rune clenched in her fingers scattered into specks of starlight.

"That was… close."

If not for Soliskin steadying her, she would have collapsed right there. Her hands were still trembling. Her heart hammered against her ribs. She knew why. The most important rune had never lit up. It hadn't responded to her deciphering. It hadn't worked at all. If the pre-set traps hadn't triggered exactly as calculated… If the wind blades had been even the slightest bit weaker…

In that moment, she understood her limits. And she understood that the gift she relied on was far from omnipotent. There would be times when runes could not be deciphered. Her gift, too, had boundaries.

And this—only this—was what she had to rely on. She had to read the runes correctly. Because if she made even a single mistake, everything would turn out differently.

No one said those words to her. So now, she said them to herself.

stories.title: Her Shadow
stories.content:
She stood still.

Students streamed past her, some eagerly debating club activities, some rushing to class, others grumbling about the weight of their coursework. They flowed past her into the Academy in an endless current, a stream that didn't seem to run dry.

And there she stood among them. A stake driven in place, struggling just to hold her ground.

This was the new life waiting for her.
 
Sigrika jolted awake. It took her a moment to realize she wasn't home anymore. She was a freshman at <te href=851069>Startorch Academy</te>.

What awaited her wasn't just runes. New courses. New knowledge. New people. A buffet of novelty lay spread before her. But the light of it all cast shadows. Heavy ones.

She still hadn't found her footing here. Just yesterday, working as a teaching assistant for the first time, she had been asked to explain Royan customs to her classmates. Halfway through, a strange confusion and pressure had washed over her, something she had never felt before. Two days ago, she hadn't even known how to make TARD-E stop its incessant singing. And before that…

She had stood at the Academy gate, watching people pass by, unable to decide which way to go.

All of it was new. Vast. Overwhelming. Unlike runes, these things weren't built from points and lines. They offered her no familiar handholds.

Sigrika threw off the covers and sprang out of bed. She washed up quickly, then gathered her things: the notes she had organized yesterday, her Bionics assignment, the preview materials for Ecology and Communications, and...

Moments later, arms full of books, she hurried out the door and merged into the stream.

She would bite into these shadows. She would find their shape, their structure. And she would wrest the knowledge from inside.

stories.title: Her Words
stories.content:
Sigrika stood at the front door of her childhood home, her hand resting on the handle. She didn't open it for a long time.

Ah... It was still hard. Hard to say everything out loud, to admit how tired she was, how unhappy. Even facing her own family, she found it difficult.

Or maybe... it was because they were her family that made it so hard.

After all, she didn't want them to worry.

"It's okay," she comforted herself. "If I can't even face my own family, how can I ever face myself?"

At last, she made up her mind and reached to turn the handle—but the door swung open on its own.

Her mother stood there, looking at her with helpless fondness. "Why didn't you come in?"

"Mother..."

"What's wrong?" her mother asked gently. "You've been out there for so long. Did something happen that you're afraid to tell me?" She smiled softly. "It's alright, we can take our time."

Sigrika stepped forward and wrapped her arms around her.
 
Something inside her crumbled all at once. Maybe it was the wall she had built, brick by brick, stone by stone, between herself and her family. Built from her pride. Her exhaustion. Her love. She had wanted so badly to be someone they could be proud of, so she never spoke of how tired she was. Never let it show. But now… she felt that she finally could.

"I've met some friends," she began. "Really good friends."

And there was so much more she wanted to tell them.

voices.title: Thoughts: I
voices.content: Hey, are you free next weekend? Want to come with me to <te href=700021>Bjartr Woods</te>? I know a secret spot there with lots of Dusk Honeypots!

voices.title: Thoughts: II
voices.content: These <te href=700026>Soliskin</te> are my friends. I know one day they'll eventually return to the Solistrees, turning into tiny sparks. It's sad when friends leave, of course. But they told me that this is their choice.

voices.title: Thoughts: III
voices.content: I've been studying these runes since I was very little. To me, they're never flat in my palm. They have depth. A piece of history, or a coordinate... like the grooves etched into Ashen Ironwood to mark the past. When I decipher them, I see projections of civilizations not yet known. What I see feels so vast that it makes me wonder. When I'm deciphering them... are they, in their own way, deciphering me?

voices.title: Thoughts: IV
voices.content: After what happened, I called Mother and told her everything. About the riddles we solved together, how I'd been scared I wasn't good enough, and the times I almost gave up. And how every time, you were there to comfort me, telling me it was okay, even if I failed. Maybe that's how I managed to overcome the version of me in the Dark Side. Mother... She went quiet for a long time. When I asked if she was alright, she finally said, "You've been carrying so much all this time." I... I never thought she'd say that. But then I closed my eyes and thought: That feels really, really good.

voices.title: Thoughts: V
voices.content: Now, I want to learn more interesting things and see places I've never been. I won't run away from what everyone hopes for me, but I also want to listen to my own heart a little more. To try things that only I can experience. You've told me about so many amazing places, like <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te>, <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>, Septimont... If I ever get the chance, I'd really love to visit them! And when that day comes, would you come with me?

voices.title: Sigrika's Hobby
voices.content: Back home, a hug means something special. When someone leaves, we send them off with a hug full of blessings. And when they return, we welcome them with a hug full of joy. The frostlands are so cold that it feels like the air itself might freeze. In a world like that, what you need most is the kind of warmth that's light as feathers. So... would you like a hug, Senior?

voices.title: Sigrika's Trouble
voices.content: If possible, I really wish we could all stay friends for a long, long time. But... I know time has a will of its own.

voices.title: Favorite Food
voices.content: Every time I leave home for school, Mother packs a huge jar of Fruit Crackle for me. She makes it all herself, and it's always so sweet. She wraps the jar carefully in ice so it stays crisp until I open it. That's why the jar always feels so heavy when I carry it… It's heavy with a warmth too big to hold.

voices.title: Disliked Food
voices.content: Have you ever tried Grilled Fern Spore? Don't, seriously don't! It's so bitter just thinking about it makes me grind my teeth... If I ever had to eat something that awful, I'd rather eat at the cafeteria! Not that we actually call the cafeteria food "food," right? ...Wait, you're saying the cafeteria's serving Grilled Fern Spore Jelly tomorrow? Oh no, no, no, no! Grilled Fern Spore is already a nightmare, and jelly made from it? I...

voices.title: Ideals
voices.content: I still want to live up to everyone's expectations! But now, I won't push myself too hard, and I won't stop just because I'm afraid of failing. Because now I know... this is the path I chose. And I want to give it everything I have!

voices.title: Chat: I
voices.content: This hair accessory? It was a gift from Father. He's always trekking across the frostlands, bringing home all sorts of strange trinkets. He used to tell me that our lives shouldn't end within <te href=700021>Bjartr Woods</te>. Well, someday, when I get the chance, I want to travel around too. Then maybe... I can bring back some interesting stories of my own, bright enough to make the little ones in the tribe smile.

voices.title: Chat: II
voices.content: When I was little, Mother would take me out to the frostlands to herd the <te href=700022>Exoswarm</te>. At night, I'd lie on their backs and look up at the stars, one by one. Mother said stars are the endpoint of a riddle. She would connect them, one to another. And just like that… everything looked different! The stars were no longer scattered pieces of gold. Each one held its own meaning. That was my first understanding of "riddles." What is a riddle? What is the solving? What is the answer? The riddle is the <ano=Rune>starry sky</ano> itself. The solving is finding the hidden connections within it. And the <ano=True Name>answer</ano>… is in the very moment you see those connections come together.

voices.title: About Denia
voices.content: Nia always says, "If you can't finish it, just drop it. Toss away whatever's hard or sad. Running away makes everything so much easier." But whenever I'm up late studying, she's always right there beside me. Sometimes I think… maybe she's actually the one who least wants to run away. She never talks about herself, so I can't quite see what's going on in her heart. Still... I hope we can stay friends for a very, very long time.

voices.title: About Lynae
voices.content: Lynae always comes and goes like the wind. Wherever she passes, she leaves behind these dazzling colors. Those colors are her riddles, and the smile on her face? That's always the answer.

voices.title: About Aemeath
voices.content: I really, really love Fleet Snowfluff's songs! But the last time she held a fan meeting, I was out on a frostlands field study... I-I hope I'll get another chance to attend! I would love to see her!

voices.title: About Luuk Herssen
voices.content: After the New Solar Celebration incident, some students said we should make a banner for Dr. Luuk. It seems that whenever someone's feeling down, he's always there, checking on them, talking with them for as long as they need. They suggested things like "<te href=851069>Startorch</te>'s Best Counselor" or "Best Doctor and Best Advisor." But if you ask me… I think I'd just write, "The One Who Always Has Candy."

voices.title: About Lucilla
voices.content: President Lucilla's classes are so much fun. When she taught the history of Royan clothing, she even turned it into an impromptu styling workshop! But getting into her classes is almost impossible. Every time the course listings go up, I have to glue myself to the screen and click as fast as I can, or they'll be gone in seconds! And on the professor review forum, her page is just full of students complaining, "How can someone who teaches everything have classes that fill up in seconds?!"

voices.title: Birthday Wishes
voices.content: Today's your birthday, right? Happy birthday, my dearest Senior! This whole box of gifts is for you! Look! A jar of Fruit Crackle, a scarf woven with rune blessings, and a fluffy Soliskin plushie… and this Sunstone I made. No matter where you are, it'll always point you toward the sun. I hope sunlight always follows you, and that every wish you make comes true!

voices.title: Idle: I
voices.content: Smile for the camera... Three, two, one...

voices.title: Idle: III
voices.content:
Hello. Mother—Mm, I'm doing well. Made a few new friends...
How are you doing? ...Yes, I know. Just promise me you're looking after yourself.
I really want to eat the Fruit Crackle you make... 
My grades? Oh, not bad! Come on, don't worry about me! Yes, yes, I will. I promise...

voices.title: Self-Introduction
voices.content: Hi, I'm Sigrika! Want to understand the meaning of runes? Need a hand with something? Then I'm the one to ask!

voices.title: Greeting
voices.content: I'll keep all of this in my heart forever.

voices.title: Join Team: III
voices.content: The runes will be our guide.

voices.title: Ascension: I
voices.content: Now, time to mark the next starting point...

voices.title: Ascension: II
voices.content: When the True Name is unveiled, the rune illuminates.

voices.title: Ascension: III
voices.content: I can see more now... So that's what was troubling me all along.

voices.title: Ascension: IV
voices.content: From something flat to something with great depth, the meaning of the runes unfolds before my eyes. It feels infinite...

voices.title: Ascension: V
voices.content: Am I... crying? I-I never imagined I would touch the True Names themselves. They're beautiful, dazzling... To come this far and see so much... Thank you, Senior.

voices.title: Injured: II
voices.content: Can I keep going like this?

voices.title: Fallen: I
voices.content: Couldn't live up to... those expectations...

voices.title: Supply Chest: II
voices.content: A reward for solving a riddle.

goods.title: Markings of Life
goods.content:
A diary dear to Sigrika, filled with the traces of her life and thoughts.
In <te href=700021>Bjartr Woods</te>, it held her joy and discoveries. At <te href=851069>Startorch Academy</te>, it holds her doubts and sorrow.
Life stretches far beyond the pages of a diary. Growth, too, never happens overnight.

goods.title: Carrier of Passion
goods.content:
A bird journal Sigrika keeps, though most entries are just blurry silhouettes. The sketches and notes brim with the collector's unfiltered excitement.
"Stay still! Don't flash me your tail, Blubbin Puffin! Stay there! Stop moving! Ugh, your tail AGAIN?! Please stay still! Ugh, again?! Blubbin Puffin!"
"New species discovered! White bird! New species! White bird! New species! White bird! New species! White bird! New species! White bird!"

goods.title: A Mother's Love
goods.content:
A pouch sewn by Sigrika's mother, filled with candies, hairpins, and little trinkets whose purposes are anyone's guess.
When Sigrika left home, her mother pulled her into a warm embrace. It left Sigrika with encouragement, love, and the gentlest of tethers.

81001412.name: Sigrika
81001412.bg_description:
Sewn by her mother for her journey ahead, this simple attire is not without its warmth.
On the day Sigrika left home, her mother held her close. That embrace gave her hope, blessings, and love. She carries that embrace close to her heart still, and for it, she gives everything she has.

name: Rover: Spectro
description: A mysterious Resonator with the power to absorb all sounds. Currently journeying to find their lost memories.

voices.title: Idle: II
voices.content: This is a testament to my connection with the world around me, and it's very much my companion now, bearing witness to everything I've experienced on this journey.

voices.title: Idle: III
voices.content: It is natural to feel dreadful of the unknown, yet... there are times when the unknown harbors hope, like how I can never know what else this power has to offer.

voices.title: Join Team: I
voices.content: We still have a long journey ahead of us. Let's press on.

voices.title: Join Team: III
voices.content: I will be there for everyone... As we head toward our shared future, leaving the past behind.

voices.title: Ascension: I
voices.content: The world around me... I can hear it clearer now.

voices.title: Ascension: II
voices.content: This power... it's mysterious, yet reassuring nonetheless.

voices.title: Ascension: III
voices.content: I still need more time to acquaint myself with this unfamiliar world.

voices.title: Ascension: IV
voices.content: A new journey awaits? Brimming with novel sounds, stories, and... fragmented memories.

voices.title: Ascension: V
voices.content: The place where the land ends is where the ocean begins. Our journey is far from ending.

charaInfo.info: With an extensive knowledge of botany, Verina is always solicitous, always smiling, and always wishing for every flower to be blessed with the miracle of life.
charaInfo.talent_doc:
Evaluation Basis: [Resonance Assessment 1916-G]

According to Resonator Verina's reports, she has had significant exposure to botanical samples since childhood and is able to audibly detect their frequencies. The timing of her Awakening is unknown.

Verina's resonance frequency shows an increasing trend over time, leading to speculation that her Forte abilities will also continue to strengthen with age. The extent of this growth is still being monitored.

Resonator Verina bears a <te href=850072>Tacet Mark</te> below her clavicle. Following her Awakening, physical changes have been noted, such as the emergence of vines on both ears and dorsal spine.

These vines form a symbiotic relationship with Verina and assist in converting her resonance frequency into Spectro energy for efficient storage and release during use of Forte.

Additionally, Verina's Resonance Spectrum Pattern aligns with known patterns of plant life. Strong Syntony reactions have been recorded during testing, yet the exact cause of Verina's Awakening remains inconclusive.

Analysis of test samples has revealed a non-convergent <te href=850067>Rabelle's Curve</te> with a noticeable periodic waveform. Therefore, Verina is classified as a <te href=850068>Congenital Resonator</te>.
charaInfo.talent_certification: The waveform graph for Resonator Verina displays stable elliptical fluctuations in the Time Domain with no abnormal patterns. Upon examination, all results fall within normal parameters. Resonant Criticality: Low, with high stability. Examination results appear to fall within normal parameters with no risk of Overclocking. Annotation: Resonator Verina's emotional state and volitional level are generally very stable, and only fluctuate slightly and briefly when she is situated away from the natural environment. Test results indicate her symbiotic plants are capable of transmitting a special frequency band to Verina, which aids her in returning to a stable state of mind. This is a rare case in the relationship between a Resonator and the symbiotic plants and serves as a useful reference for related research.

stories.title: Mushrooms 101
stories.content:
"If you're asking about Verina. Boy, you're in for a story," When asked about Verina, Riggs, leader of one of the Pioneer exploration teams, always begins with these words, "When she first came aboard our team, she was always by herself and didn't really talk to people. We were all worried about her, since she had lost her parents..."

"We couldn't help but feel sad for her. She was so young, but already had it rough in life. And she was such a kind girl. We loved exploring, but it's no walk in the park. But Verina never complained. She did all the hard work like mountain climbing and getting water by herself. She even went scavenging for food without being asked. She was such a big help to us, but we worried about her keeping everything bottled up inside for too long... what if something happened?"

"Until one day, something actually happened. And it was funny, to say the least. One of the lads on the team really liked mushrooms and went out to pick a few for the soup he made. Verina held on to that pot and wouldn't let it go as if her life depended on it. By the time we got over to them, they were already in a shouting match."

"The lad was bragging to Verina about his wildlife experiences. Hell, don't know what'd gotten into his head, thinkin' he could out-talk our little botanist! Verina had all the mushrooms spread out and started naming out all the rings, caps, and butts of each and every one of them. Being out exploring for so long, we all caught on that she was telling us the mushrooms were poisonous. She's got more knowledge of them than any of us, even gave us a lecture on the spot, teaching us how to tell them apart one by one. Now that was a lesson."

"After she was done, she even tapped on a piece of wood she found somewhere like an instructor, and asked if we understood it all. We looked at each other and blinked dumbly, then burst into laughs, which drove her nuts."

"W-why are you all laughing... Did I get something wrong? Eugh... Sob..." She was so panicked that she started picking out the mushrooms still in the pot and went over them again one by one, but we were already all clapping for her. And then I yelled, "Bravo! That's our little botanist, folks!"

Ever since then, Verina would still think of that day and feel super embarrassed; she'd put her head inside a mushroom pot if she could. But she'd still give her opinions carefully and patiently whenever it came to anything plant-related.

stories.title: Cultivating Flowers
stories.content:
The people of <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te> love flowers.

During tense battles, the military often requested extra bouquets with their supplies. These orders would end up in Verina's hands, which felt strange at first.

The bouquets bloomed for only a short time. Those picked today would wilt tomorrow. A bouquet that blooms in a greenhouse may have withered petals by the time it makes it to its recipient. At this point, the flowers would have already lost most of their beauty in people's hands, so why the need for them?

Until one day, she read the wishes attached to one of the orders. 

"In honor of my comrade in arms. He gave his life for the peace of Jinzhou, yet his name is not known to many. Yet I still remember his heartfelt smile when he received an Iris from a friend long ago. If one's name cannot be remembered, let the meanings of these flowers honor him forever."

That night, Verina locked herself in the greenhouse.

Flowers are adored for their intricate leaf patterns, but it's the fleeting feelings they evoke that truly captivate us. Verina carefully selected and cultivated the finest seeds, preserving those precious emotions in her garden.

She longed to preserve the stories and emotions associated with each bouquet, wishing for them to last beyond their natural lifespan. She hoped that by doing so, recipients would experience the true essence and beauty of the flowers, igniting a deeper connection to the emotions they held within.

It was at these times that Verena wished she could work a little harder and a little longer.

stories.title: Noting the Differences
stories.content:
People always ask Verina why she loves plants so much. It's a question that Verina has answered countless times, but she knows that people will always start off the conversations with question after question, so each time she would give out her well-thought-out answer: "When I was little, my mom would place two pieces of leaves in my hand and ask me what the differences were between them.

I would reply, 'Aren't they exactly the same? They came from the same tree.'

And Mom would shake her head, 'Look closely, Verina.'

So I gave them a closer look, and then I realized that even though they looked the same on the outside, their veins spread out in varying directions. They drew completely different patterns."

This changed Verina's perspective entirely, the differences which she had never noticed nor cared about in the past were now displaying right before her eyes.

Some flowers may look similar but grow in completely different environments. Some trees or plants may grow in near identical environments but end up taking on various shapes.

Verina was captivated by the similarities and differences among plants, spurring her passion for botany. She meticulously studied their traits to help them thrive in different environments and cultivate stunning flowers. Through this, she also began to notice the unique qualities of those around her. Just as every leaf is distinct, so are people and experiences. Verina observes her friends closely, noting their preferences and sorrows with care.

"For example, some people like to eat Lemongrass and some people don't. It must feel nice to have someone remember their preferences."

With this sentiment in mind, Verina carefully and conscientiously jotted down every little thing about her friends.

stories.title: Moments of Woe
stories.content:
Being an ordinary girl, Verina has her moments of woe, too.

Plant cultivation can be unpredictable. Often, Verina would wake up to find dried seedpods in the petri dish after a night's rest. And then after working tirelessly all day, she would realize she had skipped her lunch again. In these moments, she missed her parents dearly.

"If Mom and Dad were still around, I wouldn't have to worry about all this..." Verina thought. A hot, hearty lunch would be right there waiting for her as she walked in the door, and she would get all the help she needed in time whenever she wanted to figure something out. But all of that had long since become a memory, left in the notes that she had lost when she departed the New Federation a long time ago.

Now she would have to pull herself together and live on her own.

Sometimes, she wondered: <i>Is there any meaning to all the work I've done? Is there any meaning in the life I'm living?<i>

But then, she would always find the answer in her thriving plants.

Despite the struggle, the dry seedpods continued to produce new life and their growth whispered tales of perseverance and joy into her ears. As she nestled herself in this green oasis, Verina could hear the plants sharing their stories of pain and triumph, reminding her of the beauty of growth and blooming.

Perhaps this was the meaning of her endeavors. Verina thought as she stood up and put on her gardening gloves again.

Even if her parents aren't by her side, she is still determined to keep working hard and show them how much she's grown.

After a brief moment of sorrow, she picked up the spray can and carried on with her day's work.

stories.title: A Little Time Off
stories.content:
Verina would give herself some time off from time to time.

Verina set the flower room temperature and watering schedule. As she finished, she exhaled in relief. 

After days of work, she knew the importance of taking a break for both herself and her plants. She cleared her mind and grabbed her adventure notes to explore the streets of <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te>.

Jinzhou was a far cry from her hometown in the New Federation. No inflated flower prices or elaborate competitions here. As she strolled through the bustling alleyways, Verina was struck with a sense of genuine relief. The steam rising from vendors' stalls and the busy shoppers around her brought a comforting normalcy to this new city.

This is good, this is good. As she walked along the road, Verina thought to herself. Memories flooded her mind of studying plants with her parents, and the painful loneliness she felt after their absence. But now, standing on her own two feet, she could finally treat herself to a peaceful vacation. After what felt like an eternity of walking alone, she had grown into her own person.

And then she saw her friends waving to her: Chixia and Yangyang were walking towards her with freshly purchased Salted Milk Tea in their hands. The <te href=850086>Midnight Rangers</te> must be taking a little vacation as well. Verina hurriedly rummaged through her satchel, pulling out a few bouquets of tiny, star-like flowers from it.

This was the most precious gift Verina would ever give her friends. The selection had taken far, far too long, and while the <te href=850133>Starflowers</te> had waited for the best of times and sunshine, she had also waited for sunshine that would make her feel warm.

Now that she saw her sunshine, Verina ran toward her friends.

There was a long road ahead, and it would take some time for the flowers to bloom.

And for now, she is content to enjoy the vacation.

voices.title: Thoughts: I
voices.content: Do you know? The little flower next to you really likes you! I heard it talking about it. Plants talk in a silent and sincere language. I can translate their talk for you, if you want.

voices.title: Thoughts: II
voices.content: You saw me in the Dim Forest late at night? My bad, I was probably too caught up waiting for a Noctemint to blossom to notice you. Those plants wait their whole lives for that one bloom. I think they'd be happy to have someone there, witnessing and recording it all.

voices.title: Thoughts: III
voices.content: O-of course we can talk about something other than plants. I do take breaks from the greenhouse, you know. Um... Do you like Morri Pot? The various types of mushrooms in it are so... What? M-mushrooms are not plants. They're fungi!

voices.title: Thoughts: IV
voices.content: When you have the time, how about we take a walk together? The world is going to look very different when you don't have a particular destination in mind. Want to give it a try?

voices.title: Thoughts: V
voices.content: Sometimes, it feels like the two of us are dandelion seeds, drifting wherever the wind takes us. We have our ups and downs, just like weathering a storm, but one day we may finally land and flourish, after a good rain. Rover, as fellow travelers, let's embrace what lies ahead, wherever and whenever we may be. To me, that's what truly makes life worth living.

voices.title: Verina's Hobby
voices.content: During my free time, I enjoy strolling around <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te> on my own. Every brick and tile looks slightly different from one another, and I can find resilient little flowers growing in the cracks. The streets are always bustling with people, and the smell of steaming food brings a cozy atmosphere. Whenever I wander around and take in all these sights and sensations, I feel... hmm, is "invigorated" the right word for it?

voices.title: Verina's Trouble
voices.content: I've noticed a trend of people sharing Terminal-generated images online, saying those must be new plant species. While I understand their interest and curiosity, I'm worried this could mislead the public. As a botanist myself, I always try to be accurate and honest when I'm sharing information about plants. I've been wanting to find a way to help people tell the difference between fake images and real photos, but it seems there's still a lot of work to do. What should I do...

voices.title: Favorite Food
voices.content: My mom always said milk would help me grow taller, like how plants need fertilizer. And every time I drink it, I feel warm and cozy. Maybe that's what happiness feels like.

voices.title: Disliked Food
voices.content: I'm not a big fan of big, greasy dishes—like steaks... It's not that they aren't tasty, I just hate the idea of letting food go to waste if I can't finish it. It doesn't sit right with me...

voices.title: Ideals
voices.content: Maintaining a balanced ecosystem is no easy feat, especially when it involves regulating the population of various species. But what if we could grow flowers that have a calming effect on the <te href=850081>Tacet Discords</te>? This could greatly reduce the strain on our frontline soldiers and potentially save lives.

voices.title: Chat: I
voices.content: My adventure journal isn't just about plants. Check it out - this story is about an old lady patiently waiting for a flower to bloom, and this one is about an adventurer going all out to snap a photo of a rare type of grass. Each leaf represents a unique story that has bloomed into something beautiful. I wrote them down to remember every one of these stories.

voices.title: Chat: II
voices.content: When I was little, I thought showcasing the beauty of flowers would make people appreciate and protect them... Reality hit me hard when I saw people plucking and flaunting expensive flowers instead. It used to upset me, but then I'd remind myself: Verina, remember the value of every plant's life. Remember what mom and dad had wanted you to do.

voices.title: About Yangyang
voices.content: Miss Yangyang was curious about my plant growing skills, and she asked me many questions earlier. Then, she patiently listened to me explaining details for a long, long time. Hanging out with her feels like basking in a gentle breeze.

voices.title: About Chixia
voices.content: Miss Chixia once fed me a spoonful of her Victor Savor... I-I couldn't believe how spicy it was! What kind of pepper was that? Ow, my mouth still burns just thinking about it.

voices.title: About Baizhi
voices.content: Did you know? "Baizhi" is actually an old name for Angelica, a plant that can bloom beautiful flowers in freezing temperatures. It kinda makes me think of Miss Baizhi herself—some might say she seems a bit chilly, but I have a feeling she's got a warm and gentle heart underneath.

voices.title: About Mortefi
voices.content: Mr. Mortefi's dedication to his work is remarkable, but I do worry about his well-being... I mean, we all know how important the research project is, but a good night's sleep is just as crucial! Whenever I go and check on the nocturnal plants at night, I can see the lights on in his lab from a distance.

voices.title: About Encore
voices.content: Little Encore is full of intriguing ideas, and she always has a lot of curious questions to ask. Hmm... I've got to keep looking for all the answers she wants. Oh, you're wondering why I call her "little"? Hehe, we're just playing big sister and little baby.

voices.title: About Calcharo
voices.content: I remember meeting Mr. Calcharo when I was out collecting data in the wild. At first, he didn't seem very approachable... but then he gave me some flower seeds, all super rare species. He's so awesome.

voices.title: Birthday Wishes
voices.content: H-here. This <te href=850133>Starflower</te> is for you, and it represents... hope and miracles. Happy birthday! Sorry, I'm not really used to celebrating other people's birthdays yet, erm... Yeah. I just want you to always be happy, Rover.

voices.title: Idle: I
voices.content: Wow, such a rare species! It's my lucky day!

voices.title: Idle: III
voices.content: Can you hear it? Shh... That's the sound of sprouting.

voices.title: Self-Introduction
voices.content: I'm Verina. If you come across any plants that pique your interest, do let me know! Huh? You want me to go on field researches with you? Of-of course! It's my honor. But it can get quite dangerous out in the wild. Please be careful and stay close to me.

voices.title: Greeting
voices.content: This flower is for you. I hope it makes you happy!

voices.title: Ascension: I
voices.content: Sprouting marks the inception of a plant's journey, a tiny miracle in motion.

voices.title: Ascension: II
voices.content: As I grow, even my breaths feel lighter...

voices.title: Ascension: III
voices.content: Now is the time to bloom... I didn't realize I was holding my breath. Look. It's so beautiful!

voices.title: Ascension: IV
voices.content: Look, it's bearing tiny fruits! Another miracle, but the journey of a plant doesn't end here.

voices.title: Ascension: V
voices.content: As of late, my thoughts have turned to the wondrous ways in which life flourishes. The fish dance in the sea, the trees root deep in the earth, and the birds take flight in the sky...all thriving and growing in unique ways. You seem to always inspire me to new wonders, too... Would you like to hear about them?

voices.title: Supply Chest: II
voices.content: Are those little flowers growing inside?

voices.title: Supply Chest: III
voices.content: It's nature's gift! Let's keep it well.

goods.title: Expedition Goggles
goods.content: Verina cherishes her Pioneer Association expedition goggles, remnants of a journey and warm memories like <te href=850133>Starflower</te>. Now useless for danger detection, they hold sentimental value to her.

goods.title: Eternity in Bloom
goods.content: The flower sample from Verina's first fieldwork. She waited for the flower to bloom and carefully preserved it. Verina sees the blooming of a flower as an everlasting moment of life's beauty, encapsulating her love for both flowers and life itself.

goods.title: Notes on Wilderness Exploration
goods.content: Whenever she goes out to participate in expeditions or field trips, Verina always finds shortcuts to explore or avoids lurking dangers with the help of her plant friends. Verina draws them all. Behind a small map with childish strokes are valuable lessons, proof that Verina is following in her mother's footsteps.

The exact timing of Resonator Lumi's Awakening is unclear. Spontaneous luminescence was observed since her childhood, and she gradually gained control over light.

Resonator Lumi's <te href=850072>Tacet Mark</te> is located on her right leg. Post-Awakening observations have not found any significant physical changes.

Lumi's Resonance Spectrum Pattern mirrors the characteristics of light. When she utilizes her Forte, she can convert light into Electro energy and supply it to specific materials.

Analysis of test samples has revealed a non-convergent <te href=850067>Rabelle's Curve</te> with a noticeable periodic waveform. Therefore, Lumi is classified as a <te href=850068>Congenital Resonator</te>.

stories.title: Mountain Memories
stories.content:
Outside an old house in Yuezhou lies a patch of reeds beside a lake. To the north, the water narrows; to the south, it widens, resembling a sliced pear, with the surface shimmering under the night sky.

The summer air hung thick with heat, lulling the world into a drowsy stupor.

In the quiet of the evening, Lumi nestled in her mother's arms on a rocking chair by the window. Her eyelids drooped as she gazed out sleepily. The soft breeze from a fan brushed her skin, making her squint with contentment. The chorus of insects filled the yard, and Lumi curled even closer to her mother, lulled by the comforting sounds of the village.
 
This small place was Changzhuang. No one could quite remember why it was called that, but they grew accustomed to this name over time.

The disasters following the <te href=850075>Lament</te> had spread across all of <te href=850093>Huanglong</te>. Even here, deep in the mountains of Yuezhou, they had left their indelible mark by cutting the village off from the outside world—technology crumbled, and the villagers returned to the old ways—farming, hunting, surviving as their ancestors once had. Life was dictated by the rising and setting sun. Over time, people in Changzhuang became used to the peace and simplicity of this lifestyle.

The day Lumi was born, the whole house lit up. The swaddled infant glowed softly, catching the eye of every villager. They gathered in the yard, curious to see the newborn who shone like a small beacon. Resonators were rare here, and ones like Lumi, with such innate power, were even rarer. But in a village as tranquil as Changzhuang, there were no grand challenges that even needed a child Resonator to solve. Therefore, Lumi grew up carefree, just like other ordinary children in the village. She learned the ways of the mountains and fields—how to track wild animal traces and how to distinguish which plants might sate a hungry belly.

People in Changzhuang enjoyed cooling off under the shade of a tree. As Lumi ran through the trees with her friends, her inborn light flickered as if performing a cheerful dance. The village elders lovingly called her "Sunshine," while her friends dubbed her "Lumi the Firefly." Yet Lumi often wondered about her strange gift, unsure of its purpose. More often than not, it was a nuisance. On hunting trips, her light would flash uncontrollably, startling prey.

After being asked to temporarily sit out from the hunts, Lumi's heart sank with a pang of frustration. Alone, she wandered to the marshes by the reeds and sat down. Her glow flickered, dimmed, and then brightened again as she practiced, trying to control the light. Finally, exhaustion set in, and she drifted off to sleep. Despite her struggles, Lumi never felt rushed. 

Life in Changzhuang was slow, and there was always time to grow and to learn. 

The shimmering surface of the lake returned to darkness. The night breeze ferried the croaks of frogs away. Tomorrow was another day.

stories.title: Towards the Horizon
stories.content:
"Tuesday, clear skies. I watched the sunset from Caidong Peak! But Zhangzhang didn't come… She seems to have lost interest in this kind of thing..."

Lumi paused and closed her notebook in the golden light of the setting sun.

It was a thick hardcover notebook—a birthday gift from her parents, one she had chosen herself. Once a diary, it had transformed into an exploration journal as she grew older. As a child, Lumi was content wandering the pebble paths of Changzhuang, but now, those paths felt too small. Her curiosity stretched beyond the borders of the village. She longed for the roads that led to the world outside. 

The only problem was—no one had found those roads in a long, long time.

Her father once told her about the many failed attempts. Over the years, many had tried to find a way beyond the mountains, but all had returned empty-handed, lost, or worse. Eventually, the villagers gave up, their focus shifting to more immediate concerns. Life in Changzhuang was demanding—farming from spring to autumn, then bracing for the long winter when the mountains would disappear under a blanket of silver frost, making exploration impossible.

Lumi understood the demands of life, yet her curiosity and yearning for adventure burned even brighter. She quickly gathered a group of friends and formed a small exploration team, determined to find a way out. But despite their excitement, failure kicked in—the aftermath of the <te href=850075>Lament</te> had seemingly twisted the terrain, eliminating every possible way out, just like it had their forebears.

At first, the setbacks didn't bother them. They were kids, after all, full of energy and hope. But as time passed, they drifted away. The older ones joined the labor teams, others lost interest. Lumi's once lively group dwindled, and today, her exploration ended earlier than planned as everyone was eager to hurry home before dusk settled in.

Lumi sighed. 

She knew that for most of her friends, this was just a way to pass the time. 

She stood up, cupped her hands around her mouth, and shouted toward the mountains, her voice echoing against the rocks and trees before fading into the evening air.

The sunset blazed across the sky, casting the horizon in shades of red and gold before melting into the soft kiss of the night. 

Lumi smiled, patting her cheeks lightly. It didn't matter. The thrill of discovering something new, something unknown, still filled her with excitement.

"…Oh! I'll tell Zhangzhang all about the view when we meet for ice pops tonight. And Beihai, Ming…"

She whispered the names of her friends as she waved goodbye to the mountains, then turned and made her way down the hill, alone but content.

stories.title: Neon City
stories.content:
"You're awake? Here, drink this."

As her eyes fluttered open, her parched lips met the cool, sweet droplets of water. Her hand instinctively gripped the container, and she eagerly gulped it down.

"Easy now, don't rush," the voice urged, gentle and concerned. "You'll choke if you drink too fast."

As the last drop slipped down her throat, Lumi blinked, her mind finally clearing. She looked up at the faces of her rescuers—a small squad, three of them, dressed in similar clothing. Their leader, a girl with a kind smile, helped her sit up.

"Are you from around here? That's a surprise. We were told there's no one living in these parts," the girl said, a hint of curiosity in her voice. "Guess we'll need to update our map."

"Thank you… for saving me," Lumi whispered, her words faltering. The world she knew was small, confined to the mountains and the narrow boundaries of Changzhuang. "A-are you from the outside?"

The squad exchanged glances, and it was then that Lumi noticed the emblem on their uniforms—a chubby hamster wearing a straw hat, grinning adorably.

A hand reached out, helping Lumi to her feet. 

"Sorry for the late introduction. We're from <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te>, a delivery squad."
 
Months later, Chengxiao smiled, setting down the comb and patting Lumi's shoulder. 

"Take a look. How do you feel?"

Lumi stared at her reflection, stunned by the unfamiliar face in the mirror. The girl staring back at her had neat curls and wore a clean, fitted Lollo Logistics uniform—looking every bit the city dweller she had become.

Chengxiao, the leader of the squad that had rescued her, had taken Lumi from the quiet of Changzhuang to the bustling city and taken her under her wing. She was quick-witted, reliable, and now Lumi's mentor at Lollo Logistics.

"I look… different," Lumi muttered, scratching her head shyly. "Thank you, Chengxiao."

"None of that formality now," Chengxiao laughed. "I'm off to deliver some documents. Cafeteria later?"

"Sure!"

As the door closed, Lumi returned to stare at the mirror, her gaze lingering on her reflection for a while. 

Having just passed the Lollo Logistics assessment, she was still adjusting to city life. The city was a whirlwind compared to the quiet village she had left behind. The streets buzzed with life, day and night. Even in the dead of night, lights flickered, and voices filled the air. Walls and doors were everywhere, and restrictions at every corner. In Changzhuang, she could run free, straight through the open land for as long as she wanted. Here, every step had to be measured carefully. The crowded markets left her both energized and overwhelmed.

"Take it slow, Lumi," she murmured to herself. "No rush. No rush…"

Grabbing her straw hat, Lumi took a deep breath and opened the door, ready to face the city once more.

stories.title: Through Waters and Mountains
stories.content:
"Squeakie, I'm feeling dizzy…" 

Lumi murmured, leaning against the edge of the bed as the ship rocked beneath her. The waves crashed against the hull with a roar, and the violent turbulence made one feel like it might drag them into the depths. She clutched her hamster plushie tightly, closing her eyes, waiting for this torturous journey to end.

Days later, the port finally came into view, where the sea met the sky. Seagulls squawked in the distance, and Lumi exhaled a breath of relief as she stepped onto solid ground. "Thank goodness," she muttered. Her two companions, Tangtang and Fulei, staggered behind her, still pale from seasickness. 

"You two okay?" Lumi ran her fingers through her curls and led them to a nearby bench for rest.

"Lumi, was it this bad when you first came to <te href=850096>Rinascita</te>?" Tangtang, his head still drooping, asked.

Lumi chuckled. "Oh yeah! That's why I told you to stay fit. There are places way harder to reach than this."

Tangtang groaned, nodding. "Why did you recover so quickly? You were just as seasick as us a moment ago..."

Lumi grinned, remembering her first trip here with Chengxiao. "Trust me, I was just as bad. My legs felt weak, I wanted to throw up, and I almost swore never to set foot on a ship again!"

Fulei nodded in agreement, "The ship did rock hard. It was terrifying…"

Tangtang and Fulei were newbies who just joined <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te> and were assigned to Lumi's team for training. Lollo Logistics had entrusted her with guiding them through the ropes, but leading a team? Lumi wasn't so sure she was ready for that kind of responsibility. It wasn't because she hated caring for others; she was just worried that she might not meet these hopeful newcomers' expectations. Chengxiao had always made it look easy—could she really do the same?
 
"Lumi," Tangtang said, interrupting her thoughts, "You always talk about Chengxiao, but I've never seen her at the branch. Where is she?"

"She doesn't work in the field anymore," Lumi replied softly.

"What? But didn't you say she was an 'Outstanding Navigator' every year? Why would she quit?" Fulei asked, wide-eyed.

Lumi gazed up at the blue sky, the expanse above <te href=850097>Ragunna</te> remarkably clear. 

"Because... of life," she explained, as she had once before in her childhood. "Sometimes life leads you down different paths. Solaris is huge, and being in Lollo Logistics means traveling year-round. Chengxiao wanted something more stable, so she moved on."

Tangtang tilted her head. "And what about you? Did your family mind you doing this?"

"They had their concerns," Lumi admitted. "But this is my life, and I love it—traveling, seeing new things, connecting people across <te href=850079>Solaris</te>. That's what Lollo Logistics is all about. Chengxiao taught me a lot, and I'll do my best to pass it on to you both."

Her words hung in the air as the two newcomers considered them. 

Lumi smiled. "Life is full of comings and goings," she continued. "Some people get off the ship, others get on. But as long as there are those willing to carry the torch, our 'We Promise, We Deliver' motto will keep going strong."

Lumi stood up and gave a good stretch. Squeakie perched on her shoulder, nuzzling her cheek. "Rest for another ten minutes, then we're off. Oh, you want some famous Ragunna's triple scoop ice cream? My treat!"

"Yes!"

"Please!"

stories.title: On the Road
stories.content:
Ever since its connection to the outside world resumed, Changzhuang had experienced a dramatic change. New buildings and amenities were everywhere, yet when Lumi returned home, she felt a deep wave of nostalgia.

Perhaps those who longed for change had already departed, like Lumi once before, while those who remained had maintained their old habits and daily rhythms. The sun was dipping low, and as she walked through the village, smoke from cooking fires curled lazily into the sky, mingling with the sounds of laughter and the hum of evening insects.

Her parents welcomed her home, placing a steaming bowl of noodles in front of her—the meat was generous, the broth rich, supplemented by a spoonful of fragrant chili oil. 

Lumi dug in, the heat making her cheeks flush as she slurped the noodles eagerly. Her mother chuckled softly, passing her a glass of water.

"Slow down, Lumi, no one's going to steal your food," her mother teased.

After a deep sip of water and broth, she leaned back, letting out a contented sigh.

Her father, seated nearby, tapped his pipe. "Been away for a long time, huh? How's your work?"

Lumi smiled. "It's been tough, but things are getting better. Someone really helped me out—a hero from <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te>, actually!"

Her mother raised an eyebrow, amused. "Oh? Our little Lumi rubbing elbows with big shots now?"

Lumi laughed, her eyes bright. "It's true! I was struggling with some work stuff, but thanks to {Male=him;Female=her}, I turned it all around. Here's what happened…"
 
The next morning, with the village still shrouded in the quiet calm of dawn, Lumi left home to enjoy the morning landscape of the fields. It hadn't changed beyond recognition. It still bore the vestiges of the place that had shaped her. 

She wandered without aim, lost in thought until a gentle pat on the shoulder brought her back to the present.

"Lumi? What are you doing all the way out here?"

Lumi blinked and turned to see Zhangzhang, her childhood friend, standing behind her, smiling.

"Oh, Zhangzhang! I was just… reminiscing. It's been a while." Lumi's gaze drifted to the newly paved road winding through the hills. "I can't even tell where we are."

Zhangzhang laughed. "Yeah, it just got finished recently—much smoother than before, huh? It was once your favorite place, you remember?" She shifted her gaze to the road and continued, "Not many people come through, though. But I hear your <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te> team visits regularly." Zhangzhang paused, intrigued, "Speaking of which, have you been to any cool places lately? Anything to share? You see, I've been thinking about leaving to see the world for myself as well…"

Lumi nodded and began recounting her latest adventures, sharing the tales of distant cities and unknown lands with her childhood friend.

When they parted ways, Lumi found a stone by the road and sat on it, propping her chin up as she gazed at the sky. She knew that she had to move forward—only then would she see new things, bring about change, and make a difference for others.

As night faded, the first light of morning washed over the slumbering mountains. 

There in the distance, where the mountain path met the sky, the familiar silhouette of a Lollo Logistics vehicle, glimmering in the sun, was approaching Changzhuang.

voices.title: Thoughts: I
voices.content: Hey, I've been hearing about you for ages! How? <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te> has stations everywhere, so news travels fast! And, in case you don't know, you're the talk of <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te>!

voices.title: Thoughts: II
voices.content: This Terminal ringtone? Yeah, I made it! Thought it'd be a cool way to get the <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te> name out there… It's catchy, right? My colleagues thought so too and all started using it. Now it's ringing everywhere.

voices.title: Thoughts: III
voices.content: This is Squeakie, my plushie. Here, give it a squeeze—isn't it adorable? I made it when I first joined <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te>. Everything was new, I mean, scarily new… and I was super nervous about the job… So having Squeakie around was such a comfort!

voices.title: Thoughts: IV
voices.content: My nail polish is all chipped off… Time for a new color! When I first moved to the city, I tried all sorts of looks so I could fit in, but always ended up looking silly! Now… Now I've found my own style. So, what color d'you think I should go with?

voices.title: Thoughts: V
voices.content: I never left my village growing up, but once I did, I became a restless traveler. Riding my bike with the wind in my ears just feels amazing. I keep meeting new people, and saying goodbye to them… it's all part of the journey, isn't it? I bet you're the same, always on the move. Great way of living, right? I think... we'll surely meet again somewhere down the road. And when we do, let's grab some local food and catch up on our adventures!

voices.title: Lumi's Hobby
voices.content: I jot down all the interesting sights, people, and events in my travel journal. If words don't cut it, I sketch it out. I've filled up so many journals since joining <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te>!

voices.title: Lumi's Trouble
voices.content: There's never enough time! Delivering packages, planning new routes, catching up with friends, keeping my journal... Oh I wish I could be in a million places at once！

voices.title: Favorite Food
voices.content: Rice noodles are my absolute favorite! Spice it up with chili, a dash of vinegar, sprinkle some green onions... delicious! Next time you're in Yuezhou, I'll treat you!

voices.title: Disliked Food
voices.content: Hmm... What did they call it? Some local speciality noodle I tried during a delivery, with this golden fish broth and green veggies. Did NOT taste as good as it looked—ugh, it was so bitter! Never again!

voices.title: Ideals
voices.content: Wow, ever since we got a road in our village, things have been crazy! We've built so much new stuff. I've been keeping an eye on my team, making sure everyone's good—some want promotions, some need more cash for their fams, and some wanna travel. Hehe, busy days, but it feels great to be needed... I should keep it up!

voices.title: Chat: I
voices.content: This on my head? It's my employee ID badge. Clipped it to my hair to save myself the fumbling when I'm carrying stuff. Now everyone knows my name in a snap. Perfect!

voices.title: Chat: II
voices.content: That day, I left my village, hiked over the mountain, farther than anyone else had gone before. I soon found myself in a vast field, the air fresh and damp with dew. I was so pumped that I started to glow, and the light attracted <te href=850081>Tacet Discords</te>... Did everything I could to fight them off, then I blacked out. Next thing I knew, a <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te> team saved me, their lights cutting through the darkness, the brightest I've ever seen.

voices.title: About Jianxin
voices.content: When I am out delivering packages, I can't always find a place to stay, so sometimes I rest outdoors. Once, I woke up to see Miss Jianxin napping on a boulder on the cliff edge! She seemed... so light, like a feather...

voices.title: About Chixia
voices.content: Ma Xiao...oops, I mean Chixia, hehe! Ahem, <te href=850087>Patroller</te> Chixia's packages are mostly snacks and hero play merchs. She was so stoked last time she got one, she practically bounced out of the room!

voices.title: About Youhu
voices.content: Youhu's packages always come with insurance, full of pricey antiques. I don't know much about these stuff, but the way she handles them, you can tell they're her treasures.

voices.title: About Baizhi
voices.content: Researcher Baizhi's packages weigh a ton! Mostly stacks of books, thick ones, and a bunch of other weird stuff. Said those are for research purposes...

voices.title: About Zhezhi
voices.content: Actually, I rarely get to meet Miss Zhezhi in person… She's a night owl, barely out during the day. So I've been dropping her paints and paper at her door.

voices.title: Birthday Wishes
voices.content: Auntie Panhua's letting me use her stove today. In my village, we celebrate birthdays with steaming longevity noodles like this, topped with two braised eggs! Hey, you gotta slurp it all in one go, no biting allowed! Hehe… Happy birthday! May your journey ahead always be bright.

voices.title: Idle: III
voices.content: Squeakie! Enough playing with the letter!

voices.title: Self-Introduction
voices.content: Greetings! Lumi here! Need to send some mail? I've got you covered as <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te>' professional navigator!

voices.title: Greeting
voices.content: Don't worry, my light's got you!

voices.title: Join Team: II
voices.content: A new page in my journal!

voices.title: Ascension: I
voices.content: Is it just me, or is the light bulb on my tail brighter than before?

voices.title: Ascension: II
voices.content: To chart new routes for <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te>, physical training is a must.

voices.title: Ascension: III
voices.content: You're an amazing teacher! Didya know? Squeakie's jumping higher and faster after your pointers!

voices.title: Ascension: IV
voices.content: They used to call me Jolly Sun in my village. I prefer Lumi though! The sun sets at night, but I'm always ready to illuminate someone's way home!

voices.title: Ascension: V
voices.content: So, you are saying I'm already a top-notch navigator? Really?… No, no, don't get too comfortable, Lumi! There's still a long way to go, gotta keep it up!

goods.title: Lollo Marker
goods.content:
Crafted by <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te>, this pen has journeyed alongside Lumi throughout Solaris. She uses it to sign logistics documents and chronicle her adventures in her travel journal. 
In her travels, Lumi has crossed paths with fascinating and kind-hearted strangers, savored local delicacies and quirky snacks, and documented bizarre <te href=850081>Tacet Discords</te> that remain uncharted... even the lighthearted anecdotes shared by her colleagues find their way into her travel journal, recorded with joy and enthusiasm.

goods.title: Navigator Baton
goods.content:
When Lumi first joined <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te>, she faced challenges in mastering her Forte. 
Under the guidance of a seasoned mentor, she fashioned this field command baton, which became her steadfast companion through her most anxious days. It witnessed her transformation from a trembling novice into a skilled navigator, and eventually, a trusted team leader. 
In the dark of night, the baton's shimmering hue casts a reassuring glow, a symbol of Lumi's growth.

goods.title: Squeakie Plushie
goods.content:
A stress-relief squeeze plushie, designed by Lumi in the likeness of her beloved companion, Squeakie.
As life unfolds, Lumi faces many unexpected challenges. While she adeptly navigates her own challenges, the struggles of others can be quite a handful—each person's wishes and expectations are as varied as the packages she manages.
While she's alone, Lumi sometimes squeezes the plushie tightly, letting the weight of her worries dissipate with each squeeze.
