stories.title: Round Table
stories.content:
The light filtered through the stained glass, casting a speckled pattern across the crimson sofa. 

Dim lamps flickered softly in the misty purple room. Around the round table sat several indistinct figures. Some lounging in the light, others half-immersed in the shadows. The lady who arranged this gathering, or at least, by her position, that's what it seemed, spoke first. She had long, silky purple hair, and her indigo eyes, veiled in a soft mist, gave her an ethereal, dreamlike vibe. Lounging lazily on the sofa, she absentmindedly toyed with the sapphire pendant on her chest, a habit she indulged whenever lost in thought.

"I've gathered everyone today to discuss one thing: where should we stay? In the '<te href=850119>Illusory Dream</te>,' or in reality?"

"Since we've been wandering the edge of dreams, should we remain here, in this illusion, where everything is familiar, light and delicate as bubbles? Or should we step forward, into reality, where we might face the unknown… but also see sights we've never known?"

A lazy but resolute voice cut through her words. "How weak of you, Cantarella. You may be head of the family now, but from what I see, you're far from being capable."

A figure emerged from the shadows, a woman with long hair cascading like a waterfall. She wore the same sapphire pendant and carried an air of grace similar to Cantarella's, but with the undeniable weight of experience and authority. Her deep purple eyes glinted with an unquestionable edge.

"This meeting is pointless. Just pour the '<te href=850120>Velvet Dream</te>' into the waterfall behind the castle, and let all of <te href=850097>Ragunna</te> fall into a dream under your control. That way, we will be queen wherever we go."

"Invalid answer. Or, if you insist, it will be counted as a vote for 'Illusory Dream.' Though it sounds a little wild and impractical, I'll still write it down for fairness. This is our discussion, after all." A young girl sitting beside them answered, opening a notebook full of strange doodles. She found a small space nearly buried under potion recipes and seriously drew a neat line.

"I abstain," she said casually. "This discussion probably won't change anything. You already have your answer, don't you? For me, it doesn't matter where we stay." She closed the notebook with a soft snap and shook out her white shawl. The light caught her blue, hazy eyes.

"Why can't we just keep it simple and follow our hearts? Cantarella, you like watching the birds outside the window and long for a life of freedom, right? Then just do what feels right," said the youngest one, sprawled on the sofa, her hands lazily chasing the dust motes dancing in the light.

"This is an important decision and should be discussed seriously," Cantarella replied, her voice tinged with a hint of helplessness. "Let's start with you then. Please explain your choice and the reasoning behind it."

stories.title: Thorned Crown
stories.content:
The deep purple, venomous crown, when first placed upon the brow, brings a sharp sting. Yet, the blood that seeps from the forehead nourishes it, making it shine ever brighter. Soaked in the blood and tears of countless souls, this crown of toxic thorns rises from the depths of the sea,  symbolizing those who work silently against the chaos to support the weight of the Celestial Steed's tail feathers.

Such is the glory of the <te href=850094>Fisalia</te> family, and its inescapable fate.

But what of each member of the family? In the dark, deep sea, they suffer the gnawing whispers, until the faintest glimmer of true faith in their hearts fades, lost to the abyss. The next in line to wear the crown will take up the duty, and so the cycle endures, unbroken, with no beginning or end.

Fragrant yet toxic blooms,
Colorless, flavorless tears of poisons,
Twisted organs and venomous breaths,
Neurotoxins,
Biotoxins,
Metallic toxins…

The poisons and toxins the Fisalias so pride themselves on and the abilities birthed from them will inevitably be undone by the whispers… In the end, they only come in handy when used to seek the end of life, either for the Fisalias themselves or their kin.

This had long been the norm until I developed the "<te href=850119>Illusory Dream</te>." When the thorned crown burrowed into my flesh, the blood flew in strange, shimmering hues. Black tea steeped in mercury tasted like rich, honeyed nectar, while scones soaked in Jellyrose juice had a delicate sweetness. The heat in my throat was searing, as if hastily swallowing an entire cherry, and the suffocating sensation was like drifting in an endless sea… Slowly, the pain faded, and both body and mind became light as air. The bottles of poisons shattered on the floor, and our expressions turned relieved. The whispers were powerless in the world woven by the sea of dreams, for it gently dissolved all discord. Amidst the colorful waves, the once harsh thorned crown was softened… So soft that it formed delicate folds, resting lightly on my head. It became light and pure, like the tail feathers of the Celestial Steed.

That's why I cast my vote for "Illusory Dream." After all, what harm is there in this illusion? Have we not all wandered here for so long? Pour the "<te href=850120>Velvet Dream</te>" into the waterfall behind the castle, and let the whole of <te href=850097>Ragunna</te> fall into a dream shaped by my hand… Rest assured, this is but a joke. I do not seek to control but only wish for all to live more peacefully.

You see, the "Illusory Dream" flows within our veins, and whether we like it or not, it's a permanent and inseparable part of us.

stories.title: Jellyfish Lamp
stories.content:
In the dimly lit room, heavy with a peculiar scent, a faint yellow light illuminated an old notebook and a strange cauldron. The young woman, wrapped in a white shawl, scribbled notes in the book while casually tossing ingredients into the cauldron. The smoke rising from it darkened her clothes, leaving patches of black and purple. Her once-clean apron was now speckled, but she wiped her face carelessly, unfazed by the mess.

Distilled water, peppermint, castor bean, barnacle fish leaves, rosemary… The scent was fresh, the toxicity mild, with soothing and analgesic effects. It could treat the common Infantile Gray Matter syndrome seen recently… I'll write this recipe on a small note and leave it for Chloe later.

Hilo grass, sea okra, barnacle fish leaves, sea apple juice… The scent was unpleasant, and the toxicity potent, though it could counteract some nerve paralysis reactions. Hmm, but the side effects… Never mind, I'll keep it.

Sea okra mucilage, barnacle fish leaves dried and crushed, a splash of sea apple juice, a touch of Jellyrose juice… The toxicity of Jellyrose is too strong. Effective, but too risky.

Crush the barnacle fish leaves, drizzle with Violacas juice, mix with sea okra mucilage, add a bit of sea apple juice, and let it ferment in a glass vial… Done. Once consumed, it soothes the spirit and neutralizes most poison reactions. I should distribute some to everyone to get through the trials in the coming days. And the name… okay, I'll call it <te href=850120>Velvet Dream</te>.

The ingredients, processing method, sequence of preparation, and environmental temperature… Handle each step at the right moment, and I can brew the perfect elixir. I believe the same applies to life. At the right moment, with the right steps, most problems can be solved. No matter how illogical the rules or how brutal the situation is, there is always a way to find the right approach.

Therefore, I stepped into the darkness with the lamp, facing my fears. The abyss mocked me—reclusive, weak, incapable of adapting. Its taunting howls echoed through the corridors, the twisted frequencies of past family heads surging forward, engulfing me. Serious, rigid, pale, gloomy, silent… They knew me too well, able to predict my every move and trap me effortlessly.

But still, I played my very first and last trick as I drank a large dose of Velvet Dream in advance. The moment the jellyfish's poisonous thorns pierced my skin, I pressed the Jellyrose Medusa to my head. The violent toxins clashed within my veins, nearly tearing me apart. My soul rolled between life and death, on the verge of spilling out through my burning throat. I couldn't tell if it was blood, tears, or sweat mixed with the remnants of the potion… It dripped onto the almost extinguished lamp.

A small jellyfish wobbled out from the faint light. When I raised my eyes, the darkness lifted, and my blurred vision filled with colorful, vivid illusions.

It worked.

So, like I said, any situation can be solved with the right steps at the right time, even if you're just one part of the process. Since then, I've remained in a perpetual state between life and death, between dreams and reality. I often catch glimpses of lingering illusions, like the girl in the red hat. Who is she? Is it me? Or someone else? I can't figure it out.

Anyway, I'll abstain from voting. It doesn't matter whether it's in a dream or reality. I've been used to it, and I can survive anywhere.

stories.title: Uncaged Bird
stories.content: Since I could remember, I had always been in that big, empty house. I would walk from one end to the other, knowing every tile on the floor and every potion bottle on the shelves. The house was gray, dark, and quiet. The only time it ever felt alive was when a bird flew past the window. I would watch its white wings flutter up and down until it became nothing more than a tiny dot in the sky. Beyond that, the sky turned a clear blue, and the trees shone a bright green. It was such a beautiful sight. That was when I would wonder… what was happening in that thick forest? Maybe a princess was having an adventure. I imagined a clever princess who knew how to spot a poisoned apple. When a snake chased her, a little bird would swoop in to save her, carrying her high into the sky. There, she would find a girl in red shoes who couldn't stop dancing and save her. Then, they would dive into the sea to rescue a siren who was on the verge of turning into foam. In the end, the bird would carry them all, flying as far as it could until it could fly no more, finally landing in a castle… But what was the castle like? I only hoped it wasn't like the manor I lived in—big and boring. Sorry, that probably sounds all over the place, doesn't it? Well… Mother and Father always said that girls from the Fisalia family didn't need to read silly fairytales or have strange ideas like that. We were supposed to read books—books like The Complete Guide to Poison Recipes, The Fisalia Family's Secret Elixirs, and 108 Poisons You Never Knew About. They were interesting, but after reading them too many times, they became dull. Still, Mother and Father insisted that I memorize everything so that one day, I could save myself, or perhaps even become a Maiden or the family's leader. It sounded like a huge responsibility. I didn't really understand it yet, but I did what they told me. They were always busy, always rushing around. Whenever they left, they locked the door extra tight and checked it over and over again. I never understood why they grew busier and thinner. And why did they drink so much "water" and mumble strange words? I had learned to say those words too: "It's the glory and fate of the Fisalias." Eventually, I grew older and had to move to a different house. When I left, Mother and Father looked proud, but their eyes were full of tears. "Indeed, milord, our child has great talent, especially in brewing poisons." "Yes, becoming a candidate for the trials is the glory and fate of the Fisalias." That was the first time I ever left home. As I stepped outside, my footsteps startled the crows perched on the dead tree near the gate. They flapped their black wings and took off, flying toward a strange castle in the distance. Oh, sorry, I went off track again. What I meant to say was... after spending so long flying through dreams, you start to miss the feeling of your feet on the ground. Sure, you might step into mud or get pricked by sharp stones, but there was something comforting about taking each step on solid earth. So, when it came time to vote, I chose reality—The Other Side of the Dream, as the adults liked to call it. They always used fancy terms like that. But deep down, you already knew what your heart truly wanted, didn't you? Not just in dreams, but in reality, too. You could open the door, step outside, and go with everyone. Just fly alongside the white birds and chase after the happily-ever-after ending for everyone.

stories.title: Lucid Dream
stories.content:
In the misty purple room, voices blended together—the majestic and enchanting, the cold and resolute, and the genuine and innocent. They intertwined, forming a dreamlike symphony. The sapphire light shimmered with quiet authority, the pages of a book rustled softly, and the scent of freshly baked pastries mingled with the warmth of the room, creating a sweet, ethereal atmosphere.

Cantarella lifted the delicate teapot and poured the tea, a change from the usual. No longer the alluring purple hues, but a cup of tea with a refreshing clarity.

"Thank you for your invaluable opinions," she said, setting the teapot down. The fresh aroma filled the room. "Now, I've made up my mind."

"I will continue to wear the crown of thorns, for the poison has already sunk deep into my bones, and the dream is a part of me I cannot remove."

"I will keep brewing potions, for they are needed not just by the <te href=850094>Fisalias</te>, but by all in struggle."

"I will step outside and follow the flight of birds, into the mountains and the streets. The whispers that once trapped us are gone, and now we are free."

"I am still within the dream, but I will strive to feel the ground beneath my feet… In that fleeting moment between dream and reality, I will hold on to what is real."

Cantarella took a deep breath, slowly opening her eyes. She had just woken from a brief afternoon nap, stepping out from a hazy yet lucid dream. The sunlight at three in the afternoon filtered through the glass window, casting a quiet glow over her lonely figure in the room. The only sounds left were the gentle bubbling of the tea and her steady breathing.

She picked up her cup and took a sip. The fresh aroma soothed the restless <te href=850072>Tacet Mark</te> in her mouth. It no longer draws power from illusion or pain. This was the tea she had bought earlier this morning in <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>, just ordinary tea. The faint sweetness and subtle fragrance reminded her of a breeze in the countryside, of dew drops hanging on fresh leaves…

So, this was the taste of peace and happiness after everything had settled.

The door creaked open. She poured another cup and offered it to the guest who had just arrived. The guest had black hair and golden eyes, a presence of calm and unwavering strength that grounded the room. This quiet, tranquil afternoon was a miracle granted by no other but {PlayerName}.

The soft sunlight brushed through the room, and the refreshing fragrance lingered between them, filling the space around the two teacups. She lifted her violet-blue eyes, the mist long faded, her gaze now like a calm sea, with just the ripple of gentle feelings.

voices.title: Thoughts: I
voices.content: Can I mix you a jug of Violaca juice? It soothes nerves and eases fatigue. You must learn to relax. You can't help others if you don't take care of yourself, you know.

voices.title: Thoughts: II
voices.content: Aren't these jellyfish beautiful? Come, try touching one... a light caress. There, there, you needn't be afraid. I would never put you in harm's way. See, they only wish to wrap their soft tendrils around your finger and pull you into a sweet, sweet dream.

voices.title: Thoughts: III
voices.content: Some see in dreams the scars of a troubled past, others see bleak futures. For those confined in reality, dreams offer a sweet reprieve. Tell me, what do you see in yours, if not nothing at all? Look at you, hehe... so peacefully asleep.

voices.title: Thoughts: IV
voices.content: Dreams born of fevered escape lay bare our darkest desires and fears. The weak drown in their own fantasies until they fade into oblivion. But I know that's not you. You sip the poison like it's sweet nectar.

voices.title: Thoughts: V
voices.content: I like the way you look at me. In your eyes, even the darkest depths of the sea are made transparent. With you, I am no longer "The Bane." I am simply myself.

voices.title: Cantarella's Hobby
voices.content: You see those delicate blooms in the garden? I shall pluck them and distill their essence into sweet concoctions. The toxins in their petals, once crushed, will be tempered, the poison dissolving like a fading nightmare leaving only a soft fragrance that beckons sweet dreams.

voices.title: Cantarella's Trouble
voices.content: I've spent too much time in the depths of the sea. At times, I wish for a breath of fresh air above the surface.

voices.title: Favorite Food
voices.content: Food, stripped of extravagant "seasonings." I can scarcely recall the natural taste of most foods.

voices.title: Disliked Food
voices.content: Apples soaked in poison for too long. They become sickeningly sweet. Even the glossy sugar shell cannot mask the scent of decay beneath.

voices.title: Ideals
voices.content: I've longed to craft a potion like no other. One born of my soul, to free the dreams buried deep below, and let them soar, singing through the waking world.

voices.title: Chat: I
voices.content: Tell me, what do you suppose goes into the <te href=850094>Fisalia</te> family's famed elixir? A rare herb, grown in secret? Tormented souls simmering in unseen cauldrons? Hehe... Or perhaps the delicate flesh of young girls?

voices.title: Chat: II
voices.content: Perhaps you've heard of this method for crafting poison? Seal venomous creatures in a jar, and let them battle until only one remains... Nourished by the venom of the dead, it will produce the deadliest poison, the vilest of all banes.

voices.title: About Carlotta
voices.content: Even in shackles, she dances elegantly—a true <te href=850101>Montelli</te>, yet more than that. Where will her choices lead her family? How delightful to imagine how she might present herself when next we meet.

voices.title: About Gardenia & Rosemary
voices.content: A lively Starfish and a gentle Sea Bunny... But I must admit, I can't tell them apart.

voices.title: About Roccia
voices.content: The little girl with a giant box who plays with fireworks? A fascinating child. I wonder if bringing her into this castle would liven it up a little. Oh relax, I'm only teasing.

voices.title: About Cartethyia
voices.content: She accomplished the impossible, reclaiming her humanity from the cage of a Divinity's vessel. When the Carnevale petals fall upon <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>'s streets again, the Holy Maiden will at last be herself.

voices.title: About Rover
voices.content: Hmm, what would be a fitting analogy... perhaps an immortal jellyfish? Like these delicate, shimmering creatures roving alone in the darkness, {Male=he;Female=she} dispels shadows with {Male=his;Female=her} gentle light, inch by inch, until the end of time.

voices.title: Birthday Wishes
voices.content: Fine black pearl powder, the essence of Albizia flowers, and the petals of starfish blooms, all sealed in a glass vial bearing your name. For all the time we've shared, it has slowly fermented, ripening to perfection. Today, the moment has finally come. Unseal this birthday elixir, and look... Do you see? A fleeting moment in your long life, a private stretch of sea that belongs to only the two of us.

voices.title: Self-Introduction
voices.content: The current head of <te href=850094>Fisalia</te>, Cantarella, the Bane. Whether I am the Bane of the wicked or the pure is yours to decide. Shh, no need to answer. The moment you arrived, the ripples that surrounded you told me all I needed to know.

voices.title: Greeting
voices.content: The sea is a mirror. It reflects the shape of your soul in its tides.

voices.title: Ascension: I
voices.content: I can feel that warmth, just like the caress of sunlight tracing the sea.

voices.title: Ascension: II
voices.content: Mmm, how exquisite... Like a storm crashing into a still sea, stirring it to life with waves that reach for the sky.

voices.title: Ascension: III
voices.content: Ah... Like a fierce undertow sweeping through the abyss, causing the sea itself to tremble.

voices.title: Ascension: IV
voices.content: Who can plumb the sea's depths, or uncover its secrets? Yet for those who brave its dark currents, the sea offers her truest, most tender gifts—her treasures, her deepest secret.

voices.title: Ascension: V
voices.content: You rose from the ocean in the sky, wove through loops of time, and now you've reached the sea's depths. Remember, no matter how venomous the seabed, there will always be a place for you here. Here, the currents move slowly, and I long to... drift with you.

voices.title: Resonance Liberation: III
voices.content: Sleep, in the whispers of sirens.

voices.title: Intro Skill: I
voices.content: Take a breath, I'm right here.

voices.title: Injured: III
voices.content: I'm no stranger to this sensation...

voices.title: Fallen: II
voices.content: Like sea foam on the shore...

voices.title: Enemies Near
voices.content: Who will sink into the depths with me?

voices.title: Supply Chest: I
voices.content: We desire, and so we find.

voices.title: Supply Chest: II
voices.content: What we want has a way of appearing when least expected.

voices.title: Supply Chest: III
voices.content: Luck does seem to favor you.

goods.title: Coral Parasol
goods.content:
The parasol carried by Cantarella.

Its round canopy resembles a soft, plump jellyfish with long, graceful tentacles that seem to float effortlessly in the air. The ribs of the parasol are crafted from deep-sea coral, meticulously shaped into perfect curves that gleam with a subtle glow, both beautifully delicate and unyieldingly strong. At the handle, a sapphire is embedded, a symbol of the unshakable authority of the family head.

Violence has never been Cantarella's first choice, but when forced to defend herself, she merely spins her parasol, and in an instant, the canopy radiates brilliant light. From it, a mesmerizing swarm of jellyfish unfurls, drifting into a phantasmal sea of illusion.

Drawing her enemies into this enchanting yet perilous sea of dreams is the signature art of Cantarella. Like its owner, the parasol may appear soft and fluid, yet when the need arises, it is always indestructible.

goods.title: Cauldron of Sweet Dreams
goods.content:
The cauldron used by Cantarella, the Sea Witch, for potion brewing. The sapphire adorned on it marks Cantarella's authority as the head of the Fisalias.

She often allows her whims to guide her, carelessly tossing in unexpected ingredients, such as jellyfish tentacles, fish scales, tears from the heartbroken, and even the murmurs that linger in the air.

Whatever she adds, the result is always a pot of sweet dreams that dissolves the bitterness of reality, gently soothing those lost in the abyss.

goods.title: Potion Vial
goods.content:
Cantarella always carries this potion vial, adorned with a sapphire as bright as the one she wears as a mark of her authority. Inside, she keeps a special brew, one she carefully prepares to ease weariness and calm nightmares.

However, ever since you brought her away from the Sea of Ghosts, the nightmares have ceased.

Now, this vial is imbued with her rare sincerity and tenderness, like a soft light piercing the abyss, reflecting the gentle murmurs hidden in the rolling waves. It is now a symbol of the trust Cantarella has placed in you, the one who has navigated the dark tides and reached the depths for her.

name: Phrolova
description:
Phrolova, a Fractsidus Overseer walking the fine line between life and death, an uncanny, deadly conductor.
A silent wave of her baton is enough to attune the very frequencies of being and conduct the symphonies of "souls." The music of hers can sculpt a better world or, just as easily, summon a legion to wreak havoc.

charaInfo.info:
Phrolova, a Fractsidus Overseer walking the fine line between life and death, an uncanny, deadly conductor.
A silent wave of her baton is enough to attune the very frequencies of being and conduct the symphonies of "souls." The music of hers can sculpt a better world or, just as easily, summon a legion to wreak havoc.
charaInfo.talent_doc:
Evaluation Basis: [Resonance Assessment RA-F2005-G]
Resonator Phrolova's Awakening occurred at the time of her death, granting her the ability to tune the frequencies of her target and alter their "melodies" based on the understanding of critical frequency structuring of matters. The strength of such tuning ability is proportional to her physical condition. Latest test data indicate that under extreme <te href=850073>Overclock</te> conditions, while maintaining consciousness, Phrolova's tuning can be extended to a maximum of 30 times the normal range, with the longest duration record of 46 seconds. Due to the complexity of its origin, the exact timing and cause of Phrolova's Awakening cannot be defined.
Phrolova's <te href=850072>Tacet Mark</te> is located on her left arm. The Tacet Discord mutation following her Awakening prevents her body from aging, with the alteration in the color of her left iris being the sole physical change observed. Test results indicate that when Phrolova's body is within a healthy state, skin reconstruction and frequency reassembly take approximately 6 seconds, while internal organ restoration requires 15-18 minutes. No fatal weakness has been found as of the writing of this evaluation.
Examinations reveal a large mass of chaotic frequencies housed within Phrolova's body, estimated to be around one thousand frequencies. The exact quantity remains undetermined. Further experiments confirm that these frequencies have no negative impact on her body or Resonance Ability. Such frequencies are deemed of zero significant value and are only related to Phrolova's mental fluctuations.
Analysis of test samples has revealed a consistent, flat <te href=850067>Rabelle's Curve</te> followed by a sharp ascent and stabilization. Therefore, Phrolova is identified as a <te href=850069>Mutant Resonator</te>. Through multiple experiments, it is confirmed that her method of Awakening cannot be artificially replicated upon any other individual.
charaInfo.talent_certification:
Resonator Phrolova's waveform graph displays sawtooth and needle-like fluctuations. The Time Domain pattern frequently reveals intense and chaotic activity. During testing, the Time Domain data displayed significant distortion, and the peak value remains indeterminable.
Resonant Criticality: Extremely low.
Resonator Phrolova's frequency displays extremely low stability. It is noted that she has a documented history of Overclocking.
However, she has consistently demonstrated control of her Overclocking, indicating a potential to explore methods of stabilizing and prolonging Overclock states of ordinary Resonators by leveraging this mental stability.

stories.title: Song of Red and Black
stories.content:
The audience drowned in the performance. Some sat frozen, others trembled, swaying like reeds in a storm. In the dark, countless eyes locked onto that lone, delicate yet powerful figure, their stares hypnotized by the rise and fall of her arms, like scattered notes lost in a feverish improvized elegy.
The presto's boiling melodies ignited the burning desires in their chests. Suppressed emotions flared. Uncontrolled. Uncontained. They choked on the music's maddening climax, dragged to the edge of their sanity alongside her. At the cliff's brink, above a yawning abyss, they hungered for the blossoms of destruction and rebirth.
Yet, just before that leap could be taken, the conductor stilled her arms under the spotlight. The music ceased with a sudden, almost cruel finality.
She stood there motionless, like a statue, chest heaving. The last tether of reason that pulled her back had snapped, dissolving into the sea of emotions where she drifted alone. Her gaze was set on the ceiling, never once lowering to meet the eyes of the audience below.
Was that the end?
Silent. Perturbed. Lost. The audience began leaving in a daze. But before they reached the door, the music returned like echoes from the past. It easily hissed back to life in an endless loop in their skulls, more captivating than when it was first heard, awakening and amplifying the madness within each one's heart. In an era of brightness, people would walk out with smiles on their faces, embracing a gilded tomorrow as they drank the crimson song. In an era of darkness, the blackened song would become the final straw, leading them to the windows above without hesitation.
She never seemed to care what color her music might paint for others. She only continued to sway her hands through the cycle of time. And those sitting in the music hall never pondered where the music would lead them. Time and time again the creator of those warm and sorrowful melodies stood on that stage, yet no one ever paused to wonder what kept her there—whether it was art, fury, or grief for a love long buried in dust.

stories.title: Hidden Lycoris
stories.content:
The scarlet hall was often empty, its only occupants the Overseers' flags fluttering in the cold wind. Among them, the flag bearing the Lycoris had long since discolored, yet it clung stubbornly to its place, never falling. As most Fractsidus members would recall, the Overseers come and go like shadows, very few would choose to linger here. But she was the most elusive of them all, with the flag being the sole mark of her existence. She had abandoned everything an Overseer might claim here—no belongings in her room, no unnecessary words. She did not belong here. The detached silence made her seemingly neglectable, yet whenever the thought that she might be dispensable to Fractsidus—or Fractsidus to her—the silent Lycoris would unexpectedly emerge from the darkness. Like a sharp bloom, she would pierce the heart of the enemy, fulfill her task, and vanish once more. Nothing here seemed to be of interest to her, and few knew why she had joined at all.
There was only one place in the Fractsidus that could tether her steps. At times, she would stand on the upper levels of the laboratory, quietly observing the developments of human integration with the flesh and limbs of <te href=850081>Tacet Discords</te>, or the advancements of <te href=850073>Overclocking</te> technology. She watched the burning desires in the eyes of those who actively sought evolution, their struggles toward rebirth. Screams of success, laments of failure. As if she were seeing more than just them.
At other times, she would appear like a phantom deep into the night, holding a lamp as she browsed the latest research results. Yet she never took a single page, as if everything ended in disappointment. Those who occasionally witnessed this scene would be left puzzled, wondering what exactly she was trying to accomplish.

stories.title: Treading Through Woes
stories.content:
When life becomes infinite, what path should one take in this world? She had no answer.
The unprecedented emptiness and vastness of existence left her at a loss. In response, she chose to close her eyes and let music speak for her—untamed notes spilling out her loneliness, her sorrow, her rage, careless of when or where they fell.
The crazed genius had gained renown, yet remained as willful as ever. She outlasted every praise and insult, watching the same events and hearing the same comments repeat endlessly. Time after time, she faced loneliness, until finally she understood that seeking dependence was ultimately futile. Precious moments were often fleeting, and only those forced to stay continued to bear the pain. Gradually, her mind cleared. Then it hardened. She shut out the world, numb to all feeling. She walked alone, ignoring the crowd beneath the stage, blind to the world beyond.
She did not change her name to disguise herself, caring little about people's speculations and questionings. Anyone could perceive her physical age, but few could guess the age of her soul.
She would have wandered like a ghost without purpose forever, but what happened at that single performance offered her purpose. At her moment of realization, the unbearable time passed in an instant, as if her entire life had contracted. She desperately sought anything she had yet to comprehend, searching for any talents that would shine in the flow of time. If people believed she was their greatest hope, she would gladly satisfy their curiosity. Across countless eras, she subjected herself to experiments, enduring her own decomposition and rebirth. Pain made her feel anchored to reality, yet she could only approach the past through the gaps of pain. None of her attempts were too hard to bear, for pain would ultimately be forgotten. But why then did she feel the walls closing in? Why did her infinite path now feel like a tightening noose? Was this not the way forward? She reached out her fingers between the narrowing gaps, desperately searching for a way out.

stories.title: The Perfect Gap
stories.content:
Ancient statues were especially valuable and difficult to procure due to the unique materials and exquisite craftsmanship that made them.
Yet, the more cherished a treasure, the more likely it was to meet destruction. What seemed accidental often carried a hint of inevitability, as if the self-destructive tendencies of their owners sealed their fate.
This statue fell from the top of the cabinet by accident someday, shattering into countless pieces that scattered across the floor. The era in which it was created had long passed, and now she was the only one who remembered its original form. Determined to restore it, she would set aside time to carefully glue the pieces back together. She started from the interior, reassembling tens of thousands of pieces based on the image of her memory. It was a task that required utmost concentration, and in those moments, her empty heart found calm and fulfillment. The world achieved perfect harmony as she worked. But when she slowed her pace, the world around her seemed to accelerate. Before she realized, she had restored most of the statue. It could now function and move as it used to. But this was far from enough. The beauty of its exterior was also an inseparable part of the statue. Every adjustment, every action had to follow her will to achieve perfection from the inside out.
Victory seemed close yet distant at the same time. Every time she completed a section, another would fall under the weight of time.
Cracks would always exist.
She kept on working, putting each fallen piece back where it belonged time and again. The more anxious she became and yearned for the final result, the more the pieces seemed to scatter.
For too long she had stared at the statue, and the countless cracks on its surface began to resemble countless smiles, mocking her pursuit of perfection. They reminded her that the gap between fantasy and reality would forever exist, that she was only struggling with endless futility. For too long she had stared at the statue, that the cracks began to serve as a reminder that there was much to be done. This imperfection was already part of the statue. The cracks beyond perfection had, at some point, become the perfect gaps.

stories.title: Afterlife and Beyond
stories.content:
She looked up towards the sky. It was blue. But she remembered it being dark red.
She climbed over the fence on a search, as voices echoed around her, holding her back. "You had a bad dream," they said.
So it was all just a dream... Like the fleeting clouds above, her white dress drifted across the grassland towards town. The sun rose as usual, and the town repeated the same chimney smokes and laughter day after day... Day after day, the ordinariness sank into her, and so did this feeling of stagnation. Her music no longer progressed, and people's thoughts no longer adapted to change. Day after day...
How long had it been since anyone ventured beyond the edges of town? Where did the food come from? How did they manage an endless supply of daily necessities? These were the questions she pondered as she walked further into the distance.
Coming up on the town's edge, she saw a red figure standing before the hazy mist. It had waited for a long time as if anticipating her arrival.
Her intuition told her to stay away, but for some reason she reached out to place her hand in its palm, only to grasp a handful of blood.
The sky was indeed dark red.
She was but a dilapidated body with only one eye, covered in bright red flowers, unable to struggle or move. Why wasn't she dead? She gazed at the ashen sky, her hand involuntarily trying to grab the muddy red earth. Within her limited vision, her long-disappeared fingers slowly reappeared. The deaths of others cradled her rebirth, their residual Reverberations condensing in her right eye. It wasn't until she found the courage to leave the town and face reality that the "<te href=851026>Beyond</te>" enveloping her retreated deep into her heart. Red flowers trembled and fell, revealing new skin beneath. The echoes of laughter had not yet faded. She had indeed had a very long dream, a beautiful dream granted by the "Beyond."
But who is it to say dreams cannot become reality?
She looked up. The sky was truly blue now.
The endless stagnation and the dream-shattering mist were no more. This was a new "Beyond" she had tirelessly recreated, identical to the one they had placed in her heart.
People still called her name. And this time, she would surely embrace the real ones.

voices.title: Thoughts: I
voices.content: No need to rush off, the show isn't over just yet. The late hours of Tricktown belong to the revelry of bonfires, and the second act will begin at the stroke of midnight. Raise your arms, dance with abandon, and let us unveil the wild side of this city together. Free yourself through conducting, and let the notes forever carry the fervent, uninhibited essence of this night. But be careful, I might throw the baton your way at any moment.

voices.title: Thoughts: II
voices.content: I know full well that the differences in that piece won't go unnoticed. The inspiration for such improvisation is a gift from the city of Peyero. The sound of the city's chiming fountain was pure and clear, with a hint of warmth. When it first reached my ears, it felt somewhat familiar. As I conducted, I couldn't help but think... it was like meeting an old friend I hadn't seen in a long time. Would you like to experience it? Consider it a unique epilogue to this performance.

voices.title: Thoughts: III
voices.content: Would you care to know why the musical structure of this performance intrigues me so? The massive Ferris wheel I saw to the west side of Skob. Two cabins, locked in a perfect chase, forever parallel, much like a perfect fugue. They are bound to cross paths again, perhaps yearning to draw closer, yet forever unable to touch... How about joining in and becoming a part of this silent piece?

voices.title: Thoughts: IV
voices.content: The winds of Dolores are more brisk than I imagined. Their bite mirrors the audience's stoic silence, both filled with tension. From the conductor's podium, I can almost hear the wind whispering. It's as if I've stepped outside myself. I stand there, letting the wind scatter my hair. It blows away thoughts I shouldn't have... and maybe even me. Hmm, maybe that concert hall owner was right, and I've gone a bit mad.

voices.title: Thoughts: V
voices.content: I've said it all now... Don't overthink it. These words have been waiting to be spoken for a long time. I've rehearsed countless ways of saying them, but truth be told, they've long since outlived their usefulness. As for why I'm revealing them now... Keeping them locked away forever would be too great of a loss. To believe them or not, is up to you.

voices.title: Phrolova's Hobby
voices.content: I control the phrasing and dynamic balance through the rise and fall of my hands, shaping the notes into the sounds I desire. Through waves of pain and pleasure, I drive the orchestra toward its climax, where no one falls behind and none can escape. Until... until the symphony in my heart finds its perfect form.

voices.title: Phrolova's Trouble
voices.content: After enough failures, the sting fades, and with it, the burden of worry.

voices.title: Favorite Food
voices.content: The taste of redcurrants... the only thing that has left an impression on me. Its sour and bitter taste, perhaps? I find it quite tolerable actually. Maybe I've simply grown used to it...

voices.title: Disliked Food
voices.content: After meat is smoked or roasted, its taste is similar to... Never mind.

voices.title: Ideals
voices.content: I wish to comprehend the cycle of life by experiencing it over and over again.

voices.title: Chat: I
voices.content: Hecate has always stood at the crossroads of the <te href=851026>other world</te>, waiting, as if knowing that our paths would inevitably meet. The day I finally saw it clearly, I learned its name and understood the boundaries and choices it embodied. It stood there, silently, as if to say, "This is the moment to decide." Only when I placed my hand in its palm did I realize—Hecate is me. The me of the other world, the me of this world, and the me who moves freely between them... From that moment on, "I" became the guardian of the boundary, perceiving all, seeing even the farthest reaches of both worlds.

voices.title: Chat: II
voices.content: <te href=850073>Overclocking</te> is already common practice for the Fractsidus. I've seen countless people walk toward it, seize control, and exploit it. Of course, they are fully aware of the dangers it brings, death included. Don't disagree just yet. If you look at it from another angle, you'll see it offers not just a hopeless path to death, but a chance for a different kind of rebirth. After all, humans are creatures who seek safety, threatened by fear, clinging to life at all costs. But we... we should master not only living, but living even after death.

voices.title: About the Grand Architect
voices.content: A singular existence. A living purpose. A point of reference... Heh, given all this, isn't it comforting to openly acknowledge that he and I are both using each other for our own ends?

voices.title: About Cristoforo
voices.content: Attempting to awaken true free will in mankind, one that dares to confront the very truths of this world is an intriguing pursuit. Pity that blind will, without the anchor of survival, becomes naught but a flash in the pan. Are not the uncontrollable turns and imperfect endings caught within the cracks of the script the very tolling of a warning bell?

voices.title: About Scar
voices.content: Madmen who don't play by the rules lack elegance. With but a breath, they undo even the most meticulous of plans. I care not for his true desires, only that he remain as far from me as fate will allow.

voices.title: About Cartethyia
voices.content: Not human, yet possessing a will whole as any mortal's. A creation molded by Divinity... how I envy her. If only I could unearth the universal truth behind her success, then perhaps the echoes from the other shore would sing even sweeter.

voices.title: Birthday Wishes
voices.content:
Your birthday? Today, you say? Oh.
…
Well, if you're expecting a present or some kind wishes, then simply wait here. A long wait can be considered a gift in itself.

voices.title: Self-Introduction
voices.content: Do not fear the Fractsidus Overseer. Settle your mind. Quiet the clamor of thought. Only then can you stay and truly appreciate the perfect melody echoing through the Lycoris sea... and the true paradise that is soon to arrive.

voices.title: Greeting
voices.content: Come, let us finish this performance we've all been waiting for. Together.

voices.title: Join Team: II
voices.content: See? I haven't lost my touch.

voices.title: Ascension: I
voices.content: The warm yet bittersweet first movement is hidden in the dark night, alone and forlorn. Now, those haunting, ghostly cries have begun to fade away.

voices.title: Ascension: II
voices.content: The shadowed, sorrowful second movement conceals unease and terror. Are you not afraid? It will raise its dagger with force, tearing through the veil between life and death.

voices.title: Ascension: III
voices.content: The bright and lively third movement carries the whimsical air of fantasy. Even suspended above falsehood and unease, it compels the notes to keep dancing forward.

voices.title: Ascension: IV
voices.content: The decisive and powerful fourth movement brings forth a rousing battle hymn. Carried by the rapids, it surges across an endless land, sweeping all before it.

voices.title: Ascension: V
voices.content: This is... the final flourish. You've given it an unexpected change... Since that's the case, why not sit and listen as I play the full composition to its end? Do you have time now?

voices.title: Fallen: III
voices.content: This is far from the finale…

voices.title: Enemies Near
voices.content: Will the approaching sounds be... beautiful enough?

voices.title: Supply Chest: III
voices.content: What significance will you grant them?

goods.title: Phrolova's Music Sheet
goods.content: Her expression was calm, yet her hands waved with fervent, exaggerated motions, sweeping across one score after another. Reason teetered, then was torn, drowned beneath emotion's storm. Notes were shattered, then reborn, twisted into sound deformed.

goods.title: Phrolova's Violin
goods.content:
She was the one who received their gifts. She was the one who buried their remains.
One by one, the strings sang their exalted cries. Cycle after cycle, her bow played through repeated demises.

goods.title: Retained Concert Ticket
goods.content:
Once again, she stood before the music hall's entrance, with the ticket in her hand. She began to forget what exactly she was waiting for. The friend who understood her music? Or the path that shared a similar destination?
The crowds thinned. The doors closed behind the last of the audience. Yet, the ticket remained in her grasp.
Then came the clarity: she had waited for neither. She was only waiting for a small thread to hang on to. A lifeline she dreamed of.
She would wait no longer.

charaInfo.talent_doc: [Resonance Assessment RA2710-G] Compared with previous assessments, the Resonance Spectrum Pattern fit remains extremely high. The Rabelle's Curve shows no significant change, though a steady upward trend is present, ultimately settling into stable oscillation. The result confirms a Natural Resonator classification. The subject can resonate with surrounding air currents and gather them into energy fields. Beyond this, she can condense her Resonance power into "Azure Plumes," which can neutralize and restore the frequencies they contact, as well as erase the Resonance powers and effects imprinted on living and non-living matters. According to the subject, she received a frequency from the "Xuanling Bird"—a Remnant creature from the distant past of the Land of Xuanfang—during an encounter within the Censure Court of Xuanfang Hold. This event reportedly altered her Resonance Ability. However, Resonance assessment reveals no significant change in the subject's source of Forte. We therefore conclude that no secondary mutation has occurred. "Resonating with a Xuanling Bird... It's an intuitive guess, but the data doesn't support it... Your frequency hasn't so much changed as it has been 'completed.' To put it another way, it's like an amnesiac recalling their past. Perhaps this ability has always been yours, and only now have you come to recognize it. That said, this remains speculation." — From a conversation with a medic of Huaxu Academy

stories.title: A Record of Failure
stories.content:
Three days had passed since she told her mother of her ambition.
That evening, an extra pair of chopsticks sat on the family's table.
"I hear your child wants to join the military? Which one is it?" Over after-dinner talk, the guest sipped her tea and put the question to her parents.
"Mm... clear eyes, a pure heart. The sort who can endure hardship." The guest studied that still-childish face and smiled. "Seems you have some grounding already. Where did you learn it? A kwoon? They teach no true craft there. If you want to take the field against an enemy, what they teach is not enough."
"Come, show me what you've learned so far." The guest rose and stepped down into the courtyard. "I can't enjoy your mother's cooking for free."
"All right." With her parents' nod, she drew out the wooden sword she used for daily practice, came before the guest, and took her stance.
Who the guest was, she didn't know, only that she was a friend of her parents. But sharp as she was, Yangyang understood why the woman had come to dinner that night, and why she'd offered to test her.
Her parents stood behind her wish, but they would have her see, too, how many trials still lay between her and its fulfillment.
She threw herself at her first trial, like a fledgling beating its wings for the first time, reaching for the open sky.
...
"Good spirit. A shame your talent is ordinary, nothing like those one-in-ten-thousand prodigies. On the path of the martial arts, you could give your whole life and still never reach the end."
The instant she sank to the ground, she felt as though she'd returned to her very first day at the kwoon.
Knowing nothing. Lost and adrift.
"Your mother's spoken to me of your other gifts. Take up her craft instead, and I have no doubt you would surpass her in no time." The guest picked up the wooden sword she'd dropped. "Even so, do you still want to keep on?"
She nodded, reached out, and gripped the hilt held out to her.
...
After that, every dozen days or so the guest would call at Yangyang's home, and never left without offering Yangyang a pointer or two, now of swordplay, now of strategy. She wouldn't let Yangyang call her "Master," insisting she was only a guest cadging meals, driven by some strange whim to tutor a friend's child.
"If I may ask... when will I know that I'm ready?"
"Hmm... let's do it this way."
The next morning, a wooden post stood in Yangyang's yard. Black-gray through and through, its surface hard as iron. Even a real blade would struggle to leave a mark.
The guest took up Yangyang's wooden sword and swung it lightly. A fierce gust passed, and the blade had bitten three inches deep.
She pointed to the deep gash. "When you can do the same without your Resonance Ability, you'll be ready."
...
The seasons fled. Two years went by.
The girl's face had shed its childhood softness, and the post bore cuts beyond counting, deep and shallow alike.
She held her breath and squared her stance. The flash of the blade was like wind, lifting a carpet of leaves from the ground.
"..."
The stroke, freighted with two years of perseverance, sank scarcely a tenth of an inch past the surface.
Today was the day she'd agreed with her parents to leave home for Jinzhou.
She hadn't met the mark her "Master" had set before setting out, but set out she did.
She bowed deeply to the post and left the wooden sword behind in the courtyard.
After farewells to her parents and sister, she walked past Mingting's walls. Just as she was about to pass the first checkpoint, she caught sight of a figure in the distance.
"Forgive, Master. I failed."
"And what if I told you that you might never do it, not in a lifetime of trying?"
"Then I think... I'd grieve a little while."
"But that would not stop you, would it?"
"No."
"Good." The "Master" patted her head and turned away toward the city. "Know that this world holds things you'll never be able to do, and then..."
"...walk on, all the way."

stories.title: A Record of Beginnings
stories.content:
The walk from <te href=260009>Mingting</te> to <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te> cost her a long, long time, long enough to feel like a lifetime apart, long enough that everything she witnessed and endured along the way could shatter everything she'd thought she had built within herself.
She once believed she had glimpsed the "truth." She once believed she knew, clear as day, for whom her sword should be raised. That she could weigh "right" against "wrong," tell "good" from "evil." That a measure lived in her heart. But the more places she walked, the more she found that measure could not be taken to everything in the world.
Some held pure goodwill at the start of their paths, yet had everything ended in tragedy. Some were steeped in sin, yet sheltered the happiness of others with that very evil. The world was too intricate, so intricate that a whole life might not be enough to fathom it.
And then there came a time when she let go even of fathoming.
It was in Yuezhou. A mother had begged her help in finding the child stolen from her.
The ones who took the child were a local faction that worshipped an evil god, a pack of maniacs whose hands were drenched in sin, creatures no longer fit for the word "human."
When she stormed their stronghold alongside the local <te href=260010>Ministry of War</te>, what met her eyes was the very definition of hell.
In that moment, every thought burned away in her mind. All that was good and fair, she flung far behind her.
...
It was only when the soldiers of the Ministry of War had finished clearing the field and clapped her shoulder that she realized it was over.
She heard a faltering drip, falling from her the tip of her sword where it bit the earth. Unbinding her hair, she found the ribbon her mother had given her soaked in a red too stark to bear.
She couldn't clearly recall what passed in that stretch of time. Had she taken a life? And if not this time, then so long as she walked this road, the day would come.
She knew that if she would not face so plain a truth, her sword would hold no true strength.
Still, the taste of it was bitter.
Setting out again, she washed her ribbon clean of its stain, but not the gloom from her eyes.
Even with that mother's heartfelt thanks, even having guarded the joy of the innocent, she couldn't return them a single honest smile.
Carrying that broken heart, she came alone into Jinzhou, and stood at the heart of a square that looked out toward the City Hall. She knew where she ought to go next, but her feet felt cast in lead, and she could not bring herself to take that one step.
...
"Hey—why're you standing here by yourself? Are you lost or something?"
"I'm Chixia, a Jinzhou Patroller—well, 'trainee' Patroller. Anything I can help with, just say the word! Oh right, are you hungry? Listen, when you're in Jinzhou you have to try Panhua's Restaurant..."
...Until a frank, easy girl her own age struck up a word with her. Until that girl took her hand and pulled her off toward all that she hadn't had the chance to know.

stories.title: A Record of Friendship
stories.content:
"Yangyang, this is Baizhi, a researcher from <te href=850092>Huaxu Academy</te>. During your evaluation, she'll be providing technical support while you look into the newly formed <te href=850078>Tacet Field</te> near <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te>."
...
"Greetings. My name is Baizhi..."
"—Yangyang! What's for lunch today? Auntie called us over to try a new dish she made. Oh, but those Wuthercakes we had together last time were..."
"Pardon me, but the investigation begins this afternoon. I'm afraid there won't be time for the two of you to eat."
"Even an army marches on food. Whatever it is, it can wait till after we've eaten... and, uh, who are you...?"
"..."
That day, when those verdant eyes met the flame-red pupils for the first time, the very same thought likely rose in both their minds at once: "There's no way I'll ever get along with this person."
"Haha..." Two utterly different temperatures flanked her on either side, and yet, strangely, she felt neither awkward nor ill at ease.
It was as if she had known all along this meeting would come; as if it was written that the three of them should come to know one another just this way.
Tense as the air between them was, she thought, they were still looking at each other.
"Well then. Let's buy something to take along and eat on the way." She clapped her hands lightly and offered a middle path. "Baizhi, fieldwork takes stamina too. You can't head out on an empty stomach."
"Mm... a fair suggestion."
"Then let's try that place that opened last week... No. Yangyang, you decide."
That was the first time the three figures—blue, white, and red—walked side by side down the streets of Jinzhou.
...
"Yangyang, this is a new remedy Huaxu has just developed. Take it to Chixia, would you? A dose of this and her cold will clear up in a day or two."
"I can, of course. But Baizhi, won't you bring it to her yourself?"
"Mm..."
...
"Oh, Yangyang, Auntie Panhua fried up some dishes. Take them along. Isn't Baizhi working late tonight? These can be her midnight snack."
"I can, sure... but Chixia, you could bring them to her yourself, you know."
"Uh..."
...
And so the days went by, one after another. No memories cut to the bone, no dramatic turns like something out of a play.
Across countless days, plain as water, they came slowly to know one another, by ways direct and indirect.
"Baizhi, about the investigation coming up... Chixia happens to know that terrain well, so I made a point of asking the <te href=850089>Patrol Station</te> to lend her to us for a while."
"Ahem... for Yangyang's sake, that is. With me leading the way, nobody has to run all over the place, and the job goes quicker too..."
"Understood..." Baizhi closed the file in her hands and shut her eyes a moment in thought. "So then..."
"...What's for lunch today?"

stories.title: A Record Sealed Away
stories.content:
"Ta-da! Yangyang, congratulations on becoming an <te href=850139>Outrider</te>! Baizhi and I picked this out together. Do you like it?"
"You'll find yourself often roughing it in the wild being an Outrider, and your hair's a handful to manage. This hat should keep some of the wind and rain off. I think you'll find it quite practical."
"None of that matters, not a bit. What matters is—Yangyang's going to look lovely wearing it, right?"
"Thank you... Baizhi, Chixia."
She took the gift from her friends' hands and put it on her head.
And in that instant, she felt like reliving a scene from many years ago.
...
"...What is it, Yangyang?" At a temple fair ablaze with lanterns, her sister noticed her halted before a stall, gazing spellbound at something on the shelves. "Ah, is it that hat you want? Mm... not bad at all! Look, look, it's even got a little bird stitched on it."
"But it's so expensive..." She glanced at the price on the shelf, looked down at the coins clutched in her hand, and edged back a step. "Come on, sister. We said we'd go buy maltose candy together..."
"Mm! Knew it'd look great!" Before she could even come to herself, the hat was already sitting on her head.
"Sister...?! You can't just take what isn't yours..." She fluttered for a moment, then saw Suisui draw a pouch from who knows where and dangle it before her eyes.
"Hehe. Yangyang, you've got no idea how deep your big sister's pockets run." Suisui grinned slyly, coins jingling in the pouch. "It's just one hat. To my little treasury, that's a drop in the bucket."
"But that's money you worked so hard for..."
"Oh, what's the harm!" Suisui caught her hand and pulled her off toward the livelier stalls. "I'm your big sister! What's mine is yours, and what's yours is mine too, of course..."
...
To her, from the very moment of her birth, having a "big sister" was simply something she took for granted.
She took for granted the laughter and the roughhousing together. She took for granted the sharing of every little thing. She took for granted... her constant presence in each day of her life.
Not until she made that decision did she realize she was about to bid farewell to everything she'd once taken for granted.
If she didn't take that step, she could never become the "self" she longed to be. And if she did take it, every bond she knew and leaned on must be remade into something new.
She sealed everything about her sister away in her home in <te href=260009>Mingting</te>. And one day, perhaps, when the time came to leave <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te>, she'd seal away everything in this place too?
She didn't know. But she did know that...
...Right here, right now, the warmth coming down from atop her head was no different from all those years ago.
She knew she was no longer the little girl who'd run after her sister through the temple fair.
She knew her sister's next letter would arrive next month.

stories.title: An Unsent Record
stories.content: That encounter, that day... Was it chance? Or was it fate? When you first awoke, you had forgotten everything. Yet those golden eyes of yours tell me that what you carry, what you've lived through, may reach far beyond anything I can imagine. You always rush to the front of everyone without hesitation. You're always set on putting yourself at the eye of the storm. Is that a choice you make? Or has it already become instinct? You always... take a bigger step than the rest. And no matter how many once walked at your side, you always... end up where none of us can follow. But I don't believe there's any such thing as a soul fated to be alone. Maybe I only want to do this for my own sake. I just want to protect someone... well... someone who knows so little about protecting {Male=himself;Female=herself}. Though the time we shared may be, against the whole of your journey, no more than a single wave on a boundless sea. Still, this feeling, this impulse... It has nothing to do with worthiness or with time. It's simply my own... extravagant wish. I hope that, in joy or in sorrow, through fair days or foul, when you need someone to lean on, when you need someone to confide in, I can be standing at your side. I hope... ... Her pen tip came to a stop. She stared at the half-written letter, reading it over, silently, again and again. In the end, she folded the sheet, slipped it into an envelope, and tucked it away beneath her drawer. She drew out a fresh sheet and began to write again. Rover, how have you been lately? Is everything going well?

voices.title: Thoughts: I
voices.content: ...I thought that when I saw you again, words would come pouring out—so many that I wouldn't know where to start. But... now that you're really here, my heart is so full of joy that it pushed everything else away.

voices.title: Thoughts: II
voices.content: A lot has happened in <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te> while you were away. I've written to you about the long and short of it. Yet, some stories are just better told face to face, right? So, the adventures you mentioned in your letters—the <te href=850109>Black Shores</te>, <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>, Septimont, and <te href=260004>Lahai-Roi</te>—would you share them with me again?

voices.title: Thoughts: III
voices.content: The role of a Xuan Watcher... Though it's only a temporary undertaking, I'm still orienting myself. Sometimes I catch myself worrying about Jinzhou. But Chixia, Baizhi, <te href=850118>Magistrate Jinhsi</te>, and General Jiyan... these names bring peace just at their mentioning. I hope that one day, my name can bring that same reassurance to others.

voices.title: Thoughts: IV
voices.content: The night before I left for Xuanfang Hold, I had a nightmare... In it, I was searching for a person... someone I'd never actually met. It wasn't until I woke up that I realized that person was you. But like what you said in your letter—a dream is only a dream. Now that I can see you, touch you, and feel you... I don't think I'll ever have a dream like that again.

voices.title: Thoughts: V
voices.content: I know that after this reunion, the time will come for us to part again. But this time, our shared memories are the stories we lived, we didn't have to reduce them to words in letters. And, through the bittersweetness of our parting, our next meeting may be all the more worth looking forward to... Who knows? Maybe next time, I'll be the one coming to see you.

voices.title: Yangyang's Hobby
voices.content: My sister used to take me kite-flying all the time. She'd joke that as long as I was there, we could catch a breeze even on a windless day. But when we were competing to see whose kite flew higher, she'd watch me like a hawk to make sure I didn't cheat—not that she'd stand a chance catching me if I did.

voices.title: Yangyang's Trouble
voices.content: I've crossed paths with all kinds of people on this journey. Some walked with me, some passed me by, and some... drew the line against me. With them, there was no middle ground nor room for compromises, no matter how much of ourselves we shared. I know there will be more of this kind the further down this path. But it won't stop me from moving forward. My ideals and faith have forged the blade I carry. It protects at the same time as it cuts... Should the day come when I must point it at others... my resolve was made long ago.

voices.title: Favorite Food
voices.content: My mother's cooking... My sister and I both love it. Though neither of us can say we love it as much as Father does. After all, it was her cooking that captured my father's... Ahem—if you're curious about its taste, {PlayerName}, I could try my hand at it. I haven't quite mastered her touch yet, but... I'd probably improve faster with a good taste tester.

voices.title: Disliked Food
voices.content: Food I dislike? Hm... I'm not a picky eater. But when it comes down to it... eating alone makes the heartiest meal taste bland.

voices.title: Ideals
voices.content: Protection takes many forms. It can be stepping up for the defenseless, lifting someone out of hardship, or simply offering a quiet ear for someone who's hurting. But whatever the case may be, you must be strong enough to support others. That is why I must press on along my path. I don't dream of gaining the power to protect the world, but for now... I want to stand by your side. Together, I believe we can protect so much more.

voices.title: Chat: I
voices.content: The sword once enshrined in Xianling Village... I didn't realize until the very end that it carried a faint trace of a Xuanling Bird's frequency. Their last songs were echoes of agony and grief. But I can sense the undercurrent of love and longing layered within. It's a melody intricately woven with many sounds, a tribute to life.

voices.title: Chat: II
voices.content: I had never been to <te href=270001>Xuanfang</te> before, and yet... the Streams here feel strangely familiar. After learning the legend of the Xuanling Birds, I've started to sense their presence in the Streams... If only they still existed in the world—no, call it a hunch, but I know they shall re-emerge, and one day, the people of Xuanfang will see them soaring through the skies once more.

voices.title: About Suisui
voices.content: My sister... she's always been a pillar of confidence and reliability. I grew up following in her footsteps, convinced there was nothing in this world she couldn't handle. She's not perfect—she can be stubborn and has a bad temper. Sometimes, I catch a glimpse of her vulnerable side when she tries to compose herself and she thinks I won't notice. To the world, she wears many masks: the noble lady of a great house, a cunning rival, the resourceful president of the commerce guild. But to me, she is simply my sister.

voices.title: About Jinhsi
voices.content: <te href=850118>Magistrate Jinhsi</te>... she carries herself with such poise that it masks her age. I wonder if she feels she doesn't measure up to more experienced leaders, or to the person she envisions herself becoming. What she doesn't see is that, to me and to every citizen of Jinzhou she's ever helped, she's already the best Magistrate we could have asked for.

voices.title: About Cartethyia
voices.content: The Blessed Maiden of Rinascita, a wandering knight... I can picture her drifting across the land of Rinascita like untethered winds from here on. You see a resemblance between us? Well, our Tacet Marks are both on our foreheads. Though that's probably just a coincidence. We can both transform, too—uh, not in the same way... But when it comes to it, if I could transform into a more "mature" version of myself—Hmm, I don't think I can quite picture that.

voices.title: About Liangyu
voices.content: In <te href=270001>Xuanfang</te>, Liangyu has been such a huge help to me. Since I'm serving as an acting Xuan Watcher, that technically makes her my superior. She often wears a frown, but once you get to know her, you'll see how deeply she cares for the people she holds dear. Like soft spring rain that quietly nourishes the land, she gives so much of herself in secret—and she gets so shy whenever anyone finds out.

voices.title: About Mother
voices.content: My mother... She was once a renowned composer in <te href=850093>Huanglong</te>. Father told me she won a music competition when she was even younger than I am now. These days, she's stepped away from the spotlight to focus on our family. Some people say her talent has faded, but that, of course, is only a rumor. My sister and I grew up surrounded by her compositions. They far outnumber even Father's vast collection of books.

voices.title: About Father
voices.content: When I was little, Father always told my sister and me that he was just an ordinary teacher, desiring nothing but an early retirement. It wasn't until much later that I realized what kind of "important figures" his students were... The day I left for <te href=850091>Jinzhou</te>, he gave me a pen. He said that whether I was happy or sad, it was better to write things down than to keep them bottled up inside. He was worried that I wouldn't find someone to confide in while I was away, but fortunately, I found you.

voices.title: About the Streams
voices.content: The Streams... For the longest time, they weren't actual voices. But at some point, something changed. A faint, flickering echo emerged, like a distant, dreamlike call. Since then, I've begun to hear so much more, from both the past and the present. I don't know yet what this shift means, but I've braced myself for whatever it may bring. The wind has taught and guided me. Perhaps, it's up to me to search for the final answer. And I believe it lies within the wind.

voices.title: Birthday Wishes
voices.content: Happy birthday to you, happy birthday to you... Happy birthday to you, happy birthday to you... As always, this song is specially for you.

voices.title: Idle: III
voices.content: ...Phew, a long journey starts with a single step.

voices.title: Self-Introduction
voices.content: Former <te href=850139>Outrider</te> of the <te href=850086>Midnight Rangers</te>, now the acting Xuan Watcher of Xuanfang Hold—Yangyang. Oh, was that a bit too formal? Mm... a lot has changed, so I figured a proper reintroduction was expected. But between the two of us, no more needs to be said, right? Anyway, let's keep looking out for each other out there.

voices.title: Join Team: III
voices.content: Don't worry. Leave it to me.

voices.title: Ascension: I
voices.content: I'll learn to master this power as quickly as I can...!

voices.title: Ascension: II
voices.content: Sounds could be weighty. Jadeite could be made light.

voices.title: Ascension: III
voices.content: In the surging currents of the Streams, I hear the constant whispering of the name—"Votary of the Voice." Does it refer to me? Or...?

voices.title: Ascension: IV
voices.content: These wings will soar across the skies and the wilds, reach shores no one has set foot on before... and build a bridge that channels all voices of the world.

voices.title: Ascension: V
voices.content: I entrust this feather to you. It's more than a charm—it's my vow. Even if your journey takes you somewhere winds don't blow; even if the Streams no longer carry your voice... As long as you carry it and call my name, I will find my way back to you.

goods.title: "Shell"
goods.content:
Yangyang's hair ribbon and hat. The ribbon was a parting blessing from her mother; the hat, a gift from her friends after she became an <te href=850139>Outrider</te>. Morning after morning, Yangyang ties the one and dons the other before the mirror. It is a small ritual, a moment to gather her heart before she meets the world, to ensure she has never strayed from her earliest vow.
After her Resonance Ability changed, Yangyang thought long and hard before sealing these two lifelong "symbols" away in her wardrobe. What they meant was long since seared into her heart, and a fledgling that has cracked free of its shell no longer needs it to hold its shape. She wants now to stride boldly forward, to open her wings to the sky. Her wishes have already drifted on the wind to every corner of the world, and so she means to anchor a new self, an "adult" who can carry others' burdens, an azure-plumed bird winging in the high heavens, heralding the dawn.

goods.title: Records of Each Other
goods.content:
The letters Yangyang has kept from {Male=him;Female=her}. She has treasured every one of them, and by now they would stack into quite a little mountain.
Each letter is a journey of its own, a story they could not share in person, but chose to share in ink.
She holds these memories close. Whenever her fingertips trace the written lines—places her own feet have never touched—the image of {Male=him;Female=her} roving these lands takes shape in her mind, clear and vivid.

goods.title: The Voice of the World
goods.content: A coming-of-age gift from Yangyang's mother, entrusted to Suisui for delivery years after Yangyang left home. The sound of the tides seems sealed within. "Like moths to a flame, all who hear the ■■ are bound to walk the road of ■■■■. To the last Votary of the Voice in this world: may this journey of yours—unhoped-for and fated to fail—find some small measure of meaning through the presence of ■■■."

Yangyang: Xuanling is in <color=Highlight>Azure Sword Stance</color> by default. When <color=Highlight><te href=161001>Melody</te></color> is depleted while in <color=Highlight>Feather Sword Stance</color>, <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Feather's Edge</color> is replaced by <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Azure</color>.

When <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Azure</color> hits the target, consume <SapTag=2>{2}</SapTag> {Cus:Sap,S=stack P=stacks SapTag=2} of <color=Highlight><te href=850012>Havoc Bane</te></color> on the target.
The <color=Highlight>Basic Attack - Feather Sword Stance</color> cycle is not reset within a short time after casting <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Azure</color>. If casting <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Azure</color> resets the cycle, summon a <color=Highlight>Wraith of Sound</color> to finish the current attack and deal a fixed instance of <color=Dark>Havoc DMG</color>, considered <color=Highlight>Basic Attack DMG</color>, which is not affected by any DMG Bonus effects and does not inflict <color=Highlight><te href=850012>Havoc Bane</te></color>.
Successful Dodge can be triggered within a short time into the action of this skill, which consumes <SapTag=3>{3}</SapTag> {Cus:Sap,S=point P=points SapTag=3} of <color=Highlight><te href=161001>Melody</te></color>.
<size=10></size>
<size=40><color=Title>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Feather</color></size>
When <color=Highlight><te href=161001>Melody</te></color> is depleted while in <color=Highlight>Azure Sword Stance</color>, <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Feather's Edge</color> is replaced by <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Feather</color>.
{Cus:Ipt,Touch=Tap PC=Press Gamepad=Press} <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill</color> to switch to <color=Highlight>Feather Sword Stance</color> and cast <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Feather</color>, dealing <color=Dark>Havoc DMG</color> and restoring <SapTag=4>{4}</SapTag> {Cus:Sap,S=point P=points SapTag=4} of <color=Highlight><te href=161001>Melody</te></color> and <SapTag=5>{5}</SapTag> {Cus:Sap,S=point P=points SapTag=5} of <color=Highlight><te href=161002>Azure Plume</te></color>. This instance of DMG is considered <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack DMG</color>.
When <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Feather</color> hits, consume <SapTag=6>{6}</SapTag> {Cus:Sap,S=stack P=stacks SapTag=6} of <color=Highlight><te href=850012>Havoc Bane</te></color> on the target.
The <color=Highlight>Basic Attack - Azure Sword Stance</color> cycle is not reset within a short time after casting <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Feather</color>. If casting <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Feather</color> resets the cycle, summon a <color=Highlight>Wraith of Sound</color> to finish the current attack and deal a fixed instance of <color=Dark>Havoc DMG</color>, considered <color=Highlight>Basic Attack DMG</color>, which is not affected by any DMG Bonus effects and does not inflict <color=Highlight><te href=850012>Havoc Bane</te></color>.
Successful Dodge can be triggered within a short time into the action of this skill, which consumes <SapTag=7>{7}</SapTag> {Cus:Sap,S=point P=points SapTag=7} of <color=Highlight><te href=161001>Melody</te></color>.
<size=10></size>
<size=40><color=Title>Heavy Attack - Azure Sword Stance</color></size>
When <color=Highlight><te href=161002>Azure Plume</te></color> is restored to its maximum while in <color=Highlight>Azure Sword Stance</color>, hold Normal Attack to consume STA and all <color=Highlight><te href=161002>Azure Plume</te></color> to cast <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack - Azure Sword Stance</color>, generating a massive cyclone that strikes the area in front, dealing <color=Dark>Havoc DMG</color>, considered <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack DMG</color>.
When casting <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack - Azure Sword Stance</color>, gain <color=Highlight><te href=161003>Bated Breath</te></color>: If Yangyang: Xuanling is the active Resonator in the field, the Crit. DMG of this <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack - Azure Sword Stance</color> increases by {9}. <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack - Azure Sword Stance</color> applies {11} stacks of <color=Highlight><te href=850012>Havoc Bane</te></color> to the targets hit.
<size=10></size>

After it hits a target, <color=Highlight>Mid-air Attack - Feather Fall</color> is automatically cast.

While Yangyang: Xuanling is the active Resonator in the team, the Crit. DMG of this <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack - Feather Sword Stance</color> or the next <color=Highlight>Mid-air Attack - Feather Fall</color>, <color=Highlight>Basic Attack - Havoc in Bloom</color>, or <color=Highlight>Dodge Counter - Havoc in Bloom</color> is increased by {13}. <color=Highlight><te href=161004>Streaming Storm</te></color> is removed when <color=Highlight>Basic Attack - Havoc in Bloom</color> Stage 3 or <color=Highlight>Dodge Counter - Havoc in Bloom</color> Stage 3 ends. <color=Highlight><te href=161004>Streaming Storm</te></color> can be gained up to once every {14}s.

During <color=Highlight>Hark the Wind</color>, a Dodge Counter counts towards the <color=Highlight>Basic Attack - Havoc in Bloom</color> cycle.
<size=10></size>
<size=40><color=Title>Feathered Oath</color></size>

DMG of <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack - Azure Sword Stance</color>, <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack - Feather Sword Stance</color>, <color=Highlight>Mid-air Attack - Feather Fall</color>, <color=Highlight>Basic Attack - Havoc in Bloom</color>, and <color=Highlight>Dodge Counter - Havoc in Bloom</color> by {20}, up to {21}.

<size=10></size>
<size=40><color=Title>Azure Plume</color></size>
<color=Highlight><te href=161002>Azure Plume</te></color> has a maximum of {25} points.
Casting <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Azure</color>,  <color=Highlight>Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Feather</color>, or <color=Highlight>Intro Skill - Skybound Feather</color> restores <SapTag=C>{26}</SapTag> {Cus:Sap,S=point P=points SapTag=C} of <color=Highlight><te href=161002>Azure Plume</te></color>.
Casting <color=Highlight>Resonance Liberation - Hush of a Thousand Voices</color> restores <SapTag=D>{27}</SapTag> {Cus:Sap,S=point P=points SapTag=D} of <color=Highlight><te href=161002>Azure Plume</te></color>.
Casting <color=Highlight>Heavy Attack - Azure Sword Stance</color> or <color=Highlight>Mid-air Attack - Feather Fall</color> consumes all <color=Highlight><te href=161002>Azure Plume</te></color>.
